item.title: It seems you can forget about Peyton Manning being the Colts’ GM
item.description: July 31, 2023; Green Bay, WI, USA; Green Bay Packers president and CEO Mark Murphy talks with Hall of Fame former quarterback Peyton Manning during practice on Monday, July 31, 2023, at Ray Nitschke Field in Green Bay, Wis. Mandatory Credit: Tork Mason-USA TODAY Sports The Indianapolis Colts are in need of a new general manager after owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon fired Chris Ballard last Monday. Unless something changes, you can forget about franchise legend Peyton Manning filling the role. Despite a report from longtime broadcaster Dan Patrick saying the Colts either had or would reach out to Manning about the vacancy, ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported Sunday morning that was not the case. Time not ‘right’ for Peyton Additionally, Schefter said that even if Indianapolis approached the two-time Super Bowl champion, Manning has no interest in becoming a GM. “The Colts have not approached Manning about their vacant GM job nor would the Hall of Fame quarterback be expected to be interested in the position,” Schefter wrote . “Manning has not trained or aspired to become an NFL general manager, not with all that he has going on in his life.” Schefter cited Manning’s family and media commitments, including his weekly “ManningCast” during Monday Night Football, as reasons why he wouldn’t be a fit. “The timing to become an NFL general manager, which requires day-to-day attention, would not be right,” he added. Nothing new for Manning This isn’t the first time Manning’s name has been mentioned for an executive or ownership position. Beloved in Indianapolis and Denver, the two cities where he carved out his Hall of Fame playing career, Manning told The Denver Post in 2024 that working in a front office or owning part of a team wasn’t something “that’s anywhere on my radar by any means.” Of course, feelings and situations can change over the years. But right now, Manning has his media company, Omaha Productions, humming, and he’s still a constant presence on television, whether it’s with “ManningCast” or in commercials. Don’t expect to see him in an owner’s suite on game day or running an NFL Draft war room anytime soon. The post It seems you can forget about Peyton Manning being the Colts’ GM appeared first on The Comeback: Today’s Top Sports Stories & Reactions .

item.title: Arizona football moves up in AP poll ahead of top-25 showdown at Texas
item.description: TUCSON, AZ - OCTOBER 24: Arizona Wildcats offensive lineman Tristan Bounds (71) and Iowa State Cyclones defensive end Jack Janikowski (93) during the second half of a football game between the Iowa State Cyclones and the University of Arizona Wildcats on October 24, 2026 at Casino Del Sol Stadium in Tucson, AZ. (Photo by Christopher Hook/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Arizona football laid down some style points Saturday in a 39-3 win over Iowa State. The way in which Arizona beat the Cyclones likely led some Associated Press poll voters to add or move up the Wildcats on their ballots. Arizona is ranked No. 22 in this week’s poll, up three spots from a week ago. The Wildcats enter a top-25 matchup against Texas Tech, which dropped five spots to No. 13 after losing at Cincinnati. Kickoff for the Texas Tech game is 9 a.m. MST and the game will be televised on ESPN. Arizona received 400 points in this week’s poll, up from 136 last week. Arizona was only ranked by about half of voters in last week’s poll, but that changed after the Wildcats responded to their new ranking with a dominant Homecoming victory over Iowa State. Arizona leaped frogged Missouri in this week’s poll, while two teams that were ranked last week fell out of the poll entirely (Iowa and USC). Utah is now the Big 12’s highest ranked team at No. 6. BYU, who beat Arizona earlier in the season, fell from No. 2 to No. 8 after losing at UCF. Houston dropped four spots to No. 18 after falling to Utah.

item.title: Isak finally living up to price tag as Liverpool patience rewarded
item.description: Alexander Isak has scored six of Liverpool's 11 Premier League goals this season [Getty Images] It has been a long time coming but Alexander Isak might finally be living up to his price tag. The Sweden striker arrived at Anfield amid huge fanfare in August 2025 when he signed from Newcastle for a British record £125m. But a combination of a slow start and then suffering a broken leg in December meant his first season at the Reds became something of a nightmare - scoring just four goals in 22 games. This season has been a different story. Isak's goal against Brighton on Sunday helped Liverpool to an impressive 2-0 win against the Premier League's in-form side, taking his tally to six for the campaign already. The 27-year-old is averaging almost a goal per game and has scored more than half of Liverpool's Premier League goals this season. Like last weekend at Brentford, Isak didn't necessarily set the game alight, but again it was another crucial goal from the Swede. His strike gave Liverpool breathing space against a Brighton team that had 64% possession and actually ended the game with a higher xG than Andoni Iraola's side. In the end, Liverpool saw the game out and this was arguably their finest display in the league under Iraola, who secured his first league win at Anfield at the fourth time of asking . Only Erling Haaland (nine) has scored more Premier League goals this season than Isak and when Liverpool signed him from Newcastle these were the numbers they expected. During Isak's struggles in an injury-plagued campaign in 2025-26, the belief inside the club was that this was a long-term signing and any judgement would be reserved for when he was fully fit. Judging by recent performances, that patience is proving to be warranted. "Today, the performance was really good against a really good team," Isak said. "The first half is really what we want to be about - winning balls and the intensity." The exciting thing for Iraola and Liverpool is that Isak is nowhere near his best yet, and that should be a cause of worry for the rest of the top flight. It is Arsenal next up in the league. "Alex [Isak] is threatening, especially if we can get him in those positions and we can provide him good crosses. In this case, it's a matter of Bradley [Barcola] winning the duel and being faster than the opposition to get us in that position," said Iraola. item.content:encoded: Alexander Isak has scored six of Liverpool's 11 Premier League goals this season [Getty Images] It has been a long time coming but Alexander Isak might finally be living up to his price tag. The Sweden striker arrived at Anfield amid huge fanfare in August 2025 when he signed from Newcastle for a British record £125m. But a combination of a slow start and then suffering a broken leg in December meant his first season at the Reds became something of a nightmare - scoring just four goals in 22 games. This season has been a different story. Isak's goal against Brighton on Sunday helped Liverpool to an impressive 2-0 win against the Premier League's in-form side, taking his tally to six for the campaign already. The 27-year-old is averaging almost a goal per game and has scored more than half of Liverpool's Premier League goals this season. Like last weekend at Brentford, Isak didn't necessarily set the game alight, but again it was another crucial goal from the Swede. His strike gave Liverpool breathing space against a Brighton team that had 64% possession and actually ended the game with a higher xG than Andoni Iraola's side. In the end, Liverpool saw the game out and this was arguably their finest display in the league under Iraola, who secured his first league win at Anfield at the fourth time of asking . Only Erling Haaland (nine) has scored more Premier League goals this season than Isak and when Liverpool signed him from Newcastle these were the numbers they expected. During Isak's struggles in an injury-plagued campaign in 2025-26, the belief inside the club was that this was a long-term signing and any judgement would be reserved for when he was fully fit. Judging by recent performances, that patience is proving to be warranted. "Today, the performance was really good against a really good team," Isak said. "The first half is really what we want to be about - winning balls and the intensity." The exciting thing for Iraola and Liverpool is that Isak is nowhere near his best yet, and that should be a cause of worry for the rest of the top flight. It is Arsenal next up in the league. "Alex [Isak] is threatening, especially if we can get him in those positions and we can provide him good crosses. In this case, it's a matter of Bradley [Barcola] winning the duel and being faster than the opposition to get us in that position," said Iraola. Isak, Barcola and Wirtz turn up - player ratings for Liverpool v Brighton Isak is averaging 0.95 goals per 90 minutes in the Premier League this season [Getty Images] An impressive performance all-round For Iraola, this was a fourth win in a row since the loss to Manchester City at Anfield a fortnight ago. The fans who braved the conditions after Storm Boelo were treated to a display where Liverpool were aggressive from the outset and defended really well to keep a Brighton side that scored 15 league goals in their previous four games at bay. Bar an early chance for Yasin Ayari, which the Swede blazed over, Fabian Hurzeler's side didn't have any major chances of note. Ronald Araujo was again immense and the Liverpool backline kept their fourth clean sheet in eight league games this season. Interestingly, Liverpool's possession of 35.6% was their second lowest on record (since 2003-04) in a Premier League home win. Iraola's Bournemouth side certainly preferred to have less of the ball and this was a reminder that, with the quality at his disposal going forward, Liverpool are perhaps fine with teams coming to Anfield and having more of the ball, especially if it means the opposition aren't set up in a low block . Both Florian Wirtz and Barcola were excellent and Cody Gakpo threatened all afternoon too, with Wirtz unlucky not to be credited for the goal when his strike took a deflection off Pascal Gross and gave Liverpool the lead. Slowly but surely, his confidence is increasing in a Liverpool shirt and it is clear to see the impact he has on a game. The German just needs the numbers to improve on his end and Liverpool will hope that he isn’t set for a spell on the sidelines after he was substituted in the second half. "Unfortunately, he had to leave the pitch with a small twist of the ankle," said Iraola. "It doesn't look very big but we are playing every three days so we need to see where he is." As for Barcola, there is a style to his play that can energise a crowd and the way he won possession for Isak's goal felt like it ticked off exactly what Iraola wanted with the high press and sheer desire to win the ball back. That left Isak to finish instinctively and Barcola imitated Isak's celebration, just like they did last weekend in west London, as Liverpool moved up to fourth. Theirs is a combination that cost the Reds a total of £248m but if they can keep on combining and winning games, that will do just fine for Iraola and Liverpool. item.title: SC Freiburg vs. Bayern Munich: Gamethread
item.description: Photo by Alex Grimm/Getty Images | Getty Images 82’ — Goal. Freiburg score a lucky goal to bring the game to one goal. Bayern still 2-1 up. The goal is credited as a Tom Bischof own goal. 81’ — Saibari and Kane shoot bullets at the Freiburg goal, but Backhaus somehow keeps both of them out. 76’ — Upamecano heads the ball just over from a corner kick by Olise. 75’ — Saibari is forced into a tight angle, his shot is therefore a tame one. 73’ — Alphonso Davies replaces Nathaniel Brown. 69’ — Brown shoots weakly at Backhaus. 62’ — Saibari’s first shot in the game is saved by Backhaus. 61’ — Ismael Saibari and Sacha Boey come on for Serge Gnabry and Josip Stanisic. 59’ — Urbig collects Igor Matanović‘s shot. 57’ — Harry Kane heads the ball over from an Olise freekick. 55’ — Jan-Niklas Beste gets booked for a sliding challenge on Brown. 52’ — Upamecano nearly pokes the ball home from a corner kick. 47’ — Derry Scherhant shoots the freekick straight at Jonas Urbig, who collects the ball. 46’ — Welcome back! The second half has begun. Halftime Observations Solid game from Bayern so far. The counterattacking scheme has somewhat worked, presumably another system the team is trying out for future use. That was an incredible goal by Dayot Upamecano. Won the ball outside his box, ran up and latched onto Michael Olise’s pass and finished a 1v1. Harry Kane probably taught him a thing or two. Lennart Karl is frustrating to watch at times, and today is one of those times. Konrad Laimer is obviously trying to get used to playing in midfield again after an extended period of playing as a right-back. 45+5’ — Half time! 45+3’ — Höler sees Jonas Urbig off his line and tries to shoot from his own half. The ball goes out. 45’ — Four minutes of stoppage time added on. 43’ — TOR! Serge Gnabry shoots from an impossible angle to put Bayern 2-0 up just before the break. 42’ — Gnabry fires WAY over the goal. 34’ — Nathaniel Brown’s shot gets saved by Backhaus. 29’ — Yuito Suzuki tries his luck from distance, but it goes over. 27’ — Serge Gnabry fires wide of the target. 25’ — Lucas Höler gets a yellow card. 24’ — Michael Olise dribbles inside but hits his shot weakly at Backhaus. 22’ — Freiburg could not poke the ball home after a scramble inside Bayern’s box. 16’ — TOR! After a quick exchange of attacks, Bayern go on the counterattack and Dayot Upamecano of all people finishes 1v1 against Mio Backhaus. Bayern go 1-0 up! 14’ — Bayern under pressure from the home side. 4’ — The game has resumed. 1’ — Not even a minute in, and the game is temporarily suspended because of pyro smoke. Kickoff — LET’S GOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOO! Lineups are out! Tom Bischof and Konrad Laimer start in midfield, with Nathaniel Brown, Lennart Karl and Jonas Urbig joining the starting XI. Alphonso Davies, Ismael Saibari, and Tim Binder start on the bench. item.title: ‘WNBA has some problem solving to do’: WNBA faces a major problem before Game 6
item.description: Aug 31, 2025; San Francisco, California, USA; Golden State Valkyries guard Kaitlyn Chen (2) holds a ball as the WNBA logo appears on the ball and shorts before the game against the Indiana Fever at Chase Center. Mandatory Credit: Darren Yamashita-Imagn Images The Golden State Valkyries’ 67-62 win over the Atlanta Dream on Saturday evened the WNBA Finals at 2-2, guaranteeing that the series will go at least six games. But that has created a major headache for the league. Game 6 is scheduled to be played in Atlanta on Thursday night, but there’s one big problem: the Dream’s preferred arena is already booked. The Atlanta Hawks are set to play at State Farm Arena that same night, and the Hawks’ CEO has made it clear that it’s up to the WNBA to fix it, even urging fans to “write your congressman.” Dream’s Arena Issues The Dream’s regular home is Gateway Center Arena in College Park, which seats just 3,500 fans, the smallest venue in the league. But Atlanta has played all of its postseason home games at State Farm Arena, which it shares with the Hawks. That arrangement has already caused some scheduling issues. Game 3 was moved up a day to avoid a concert, and Game 4 was moved to a 1 p.m. ET tip-off to make room for the Hawks’ home opener that night. The Dream have since announced a multi-year deal to play all of their home games at State Farm Arena beginning in 2027. But that doesn’t help them this week. ‘Write Your Congressman’ Game 6 is scheduled for Thursday at 8 p.m. ET, but its location is still listed as “TBD.” That’s because the Hawks host the Cleveland Cavaliers at State Farm Arena at 7 p.m. ET that same night, according to CBS Sports’ Jack Maloney . Hawks CEO Steve Koonin said that the arena has offered up several other dates, but that the decision is in the league’s hands. “Hawks CEO Steve Koonin tells @929TheGame that State Farm Arena has made multiple dates available for a potential WNBA Finals Game Six, but rescheduling that game is solely a league decision,” wrote Mike Conti of 92.9 The Game. “He encouraged fans to ‘write your congressman’ to urge a schedule change.” After Saturday’s game, Conti added, “Game Six is now necessary, and the WNBA has some problem solving to do,” on X . No Easy Fix None of the options are simple. Moving Game 6 to Wednesday won’t work because the Hawks host the Miami Heat that night, and moving it to Friday would set up a back-to-back with Game 7, which is scheduled for Saturday in San Francisco. Game 7 can’t be easily moved either, as Conti noted that the Golden State Warriors have home games on Nov. 1 and Nov. 2. State Farm Arena is open on Friday, so the Hawks-Cavaliers game could be moved, but that would require sign-off from the NBA, both teams, and broadcast partners. The Dream could also return to Gateway Center, though its capacity is far below Finals standards. Dream star Angel Reese made her preference clear. “Being able to come here and play in front of the home crowd again would be amazing,” Reese

The Dream could also return to Gateway Center, though its capacity is far below Finals standards. Dream star Angel Reese made her preference clear. “Being able to come here and play in front of the home crowd again would be amazing,” Reese said, via CBS Sports . The WNBA doesn’t have much time to figure this out. Game 5 is Monday in San Francisco. The post ‘WNBA has some problem solving to do’: WNBA faces a major problem before Game 6 appeared first on The Comeback: Today’s Top Sports Stories & Reactions .

item.title: Clemson’s Dabo Swinney throws shade at refs after ‘disturbing’ loss to Virginia Tech
item.description: Butch Dill-Imagn Images Clemson’s Dabo Swinney throws shade at refs after ‘disturbing’ loss to Virginia Tech appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Clemson Tigers are 4-3 on the season after suffering a 20-16 Week 8 loss to the Virginia Tech Hokies. While the team didn’t play all that well on Saturday, there was a controversial moment where officials waved off wide receiver Bryant Wesco Jr.’s catch late in the contest that would have turned out to be a favorable play for the Tigers. It’s safe to say that Dabo Swinney was not happy with those calls. The 56-year-old head coach went on a little rant during his postgame press conference, ripping the officials for allegedly not getting the call right despite having time to rewatch the play, according to Chapel Fowler of The State Newspaper. While Swinney was upset with the call, he ultimately took full ownership of the loss. “They said he didn’t possess it, so that’s what happened,” Swinney said. On the refs: “They were very visible. They had a lot of TV time tonight, but we didn’t control what we needed to control… It’s disturbing that we didn’t do some of the routine stuff well and frustrating because we didn’t do enough to help them as coaches. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “We’ve got a resilient group of guys, an amazing group of young people that are encouraging me. … We’ll regroup,” Swinney continued. Says that although you “may have to shift some of your (season) goals” now, their No. 1 goal is still to just win the next one. “Clemson coach Dabo Swinney says the fact they’ve lost so much at home recently ‘bothers me’ and hurts a little extra,” Fowler wrote on X. “Dabo: ‘But we’ll turn it around.'” The public seemingly thought the officiating for the Virginia Tech-Clemson game was a bit sloppy as well. While the veteran head coach wasn’t happy with some of the calls, Dabo Swinney does appear ready to put the game in the rearview mirror and focus on the schedule ahead. The Tigers move on to Week 9, where the team will face off against the Florida State Seminoles on the road. Related: TCU fires coach after West Virginia loss, but it’s not Sonny Dykes Related: Oregon football fires offensive coordinator after another dismal performance vs. Illinois

item.title: Vikings legend Cris Carter makes Kyler Murray guarantee after handing out early grade
item.description: Image credit: Brad Rempel-Imagn Images Vikings legend Cris Carter makes Kyler Murray guarantee after handing out early grade appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Minnesota Vikings will look to push their record to 6-0 on Sunday afternoon when they play host to the Indianapolis Colts. While the Vikings have been mightily impressive in winning every game so far, they’ve still seen some underwhelming play from veteran Kyler Murray at the quarterback position. Recently, Vikings legendary wide receiver Cris Carter spoke on his confidence level that Murray will be able to turn things around moving forward. “All the quarterbacks that have played under KOC, you see them getting better, and a lot of them did not have the overall ball talent or speed and ability to get out of the pocket… As they start getting some of these players back, get that running attack back, I see him only getting better as the season moves on,” he said, per DJ Siddiqi of RG. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) However, he was also honest in giving Murray a rating for his performance so far this season. “I would say it’s still too early. I would probably give him a C (against the Saints). Him running might get him a B-minus and everything, but I think it’s only going to get better when they get the wide receiving corps healthy,” he said. Indeed, the Vikings have been playing without several key skill positional players, with Justin Jefferson among those having missed time so far in 2026. Murray has looked shaky at times, although, as Carter mentioned, Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell has a track record of getting elite play out of his quarterbacks sooner rather than later. In any case, Minnesota and Indianapolis are slated to kick things off on Sunday at 1:00 pm ET. Related: Vikings planning big Jordan Mason decision ahead of Week 7 Related: Vikings’ perfect Saquon Barkley trade offer to Eagles before NFL trade deadline

item.title: Rutgers Listed as 14.5 Point Underdogs Against Michigan
item.description: ANN ARBOR, MICHIGAN - SEPTEMBER 23: Roman Wilson #1 of the Michigan Wolverines looks for yards after a second half catch next to Robert Longerbeam #7 of the Rutgers Scarlet Knights at Michigan Stadium on September 23, 2023 in Ann Arbor, Michigan. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images After suffering a 42-14 loss to No.24 Northwestern on the road, Rutgers football will return home to play Michigan this Saturday in a game where they are currently listed as the underdog by 14.5 points, according to FanDuel . Michigan will also be coming into this game after a loss, falling to No.6 Indiana 13-6 in overtime yesterday. The over/under is currently set at 47.5, one of the lowest for a Rutgers game this season. The Wolverines and the Scarlet Knights are an interesting matchup because it pits a bad Michigan offense against a really poor Rutgers defense. Michigan averages 20.3 points per game, which is No. 108 in the FBS. Rutgers surrenders 37.7 points per game, which is No. 128 in the FBS. Rutgers surrenders 6 yards per rush, which is the third-worst in the FBS, while Michigan averages 3.7 yards per rush, which is No. 96 in the FBS. The Wolverines average 165.9 passing yards per game, which is No.125 in the FBS, while Rutgers allows an average of 245.3 passing yards per game, which ranks 100th in the FBS. Michigan has only scored more than 20 points twice this season while Rutgers has only held two opponents under 30 points this season. The stoppable force vs the moveable object. On the flip side, however, Michigan has a stellar defense that will prove extremely difficult for Rutgers to punch through. Currently, they surrender an average of 15.7 points per game, which is 11th in the FBS. Michigan defensive end John Henry Daley could be a huge issue for the Knights, as he has recorded four sacks on the season so far, and Rutgers has struggled to keep defenders off of their quarterback all season. They as a team also average 1.3 positive turnovers per game, which could be a huge issue given the Knights’ turnover issues. The final wrinkle in this matchup for both teams is the quarterback. Michigan last week started Tommy Carr over Bryce Underwood. Carr threw for 167 yards, no touchdowns, and one interception. It will be interesting to see how he improves from his first start to his second start. Rutgers, on the other hand, saw three quarterbacks take the field, none of whom performed well. Starting quarterback Dylan Lonergan was knocked out of the game before he could attempt a pass, while backups AJ Surace and Sean Ashenfelder combined completed 9 out of 27 pass attempts for 100 yards, no touchdowns and two interceptions. Lonergan gives Rutgers its best chance to stay competitive, but if he is unable to go, whoever replaces him will have the tall task of facing one of the strongest defenses in the Big Ten. Rutgers vs. Michigan will kick off inside SHI Stadium on Halloween, Oct. 31, at 12:30. Live coverage will be available on the Big Ten Netw

item.title: No. 1 Maryland field hockey’s defense silences No. 11 Indiana in 1-0 victory
item.description: On Sunday afternoon in Bloomington, Indiana, No. 1 Maryland field hockey found itself in a defensive duel with No. 13 Indiana in a game with Big Ten tournament implications. The scoreless deadlock remained for nearly 40 minutes until Maryland junior Babs van Hest cracked the code with her ninth goal of the season. For the final 20 minutes, Maryland’s defense kept Indiana quiet to ensure a 1-0 victory. Like most games, Maryland controlled the battle for possession in the first quarter. The Terps frequently found themselves within the 23-meter line, but the Hoosiers’ defense packed the shooting circle to close off shooting lanes. Indiana picked up some momentum towards the end of the opening frame. On one particular chance, Molly Stutte found herself behind Maryland’s defense, but Terps goalkeeper Alyssa Klebasko made a kick save to put an end to the threat. To start the second quarter, Indiana pressed Maryland’s defense, nearly breaking through with multiple chances on the doorstep. However, Klebasko nicely navigated the chaos within the shooting circle to keep the match scoreless halfway through the period. The Hoosiers continued to frustrate the Terps before halftime. Indiana denied Maryland on a pair of penalty corners before generating a pair of its own. Fortunately for the Terps, Klebasko was on her game, as the senior picked up three first-half saves. On Thursday, Maryland was burned when it was whistled for a card. On Sunday, the Terps found themselves on the right side of a man-advantage. As time ticked down on an Indiana green card, van Hest corralled a loose ball in the circle and smashed a shot to the back of the net to give the Terps a third-quarter lead they wouldn’t relinquish. The goal broke a Maryland scoring drought that nearly reached four quarters. On the other side, Maryland held Indiana shotless in the third quarter. It was the fifth straight contest the Terps kept their opponent without a shot in a quarter. Maryland’s strong defensive play remained in the final frame, as the Terps neutralized Indiana’s attack. The Hoosiers brought on an extra attacker in favor of the goalie with over five minutes to play, but the Terps weren’t fazed, as Indiana failed to record a single shot in the final stretch of the game. Maryland returns to College Park for its final game of the regular season Friday. The Terps will host No. 6 Iowa. Three things to know 1. Brilliant Babs. Babs van Hest’s ninth goal of the season ties her with Francisca Eschoyez for the team lead. 2. Stacking up the shutouts. The Terps registered their ninth clean sheet of the season and their third in four games on Sunday. 3. Tournament update. Maryland’s win puts itself in prime position to earn the No. 2 seed in the Big Ten tournament. Another win on Friday against Iowa would confirm the No. 2 seed for good. item.title: Michigan football’s Kyle Whittingham still grossed out by nonexistent offense even after Tommy Carr move
item.description: Junfu Han / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images Michigan football’s Kyle Whittingham still grossed out by nonexistent offense even after Tommy Carr move appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . On Saturday afternoon, the Michigan football program dropped to 4-3 with a narrow home loss in overtime to the defending national champion Indiana Hoosiers. The Wolverines stuck around all game in this one, having some chances late in the fourth quarter to potentially come away with a win, but as has been the case so often this season, Michigan’s offense wasn’t able to make enough plays down the stretch to get the win. After the game, Wolverines head coach Kyle Whittingham kept it real amid the ugly offensive performance. “That was disappointing to say the least.. They’re an outstanding defense, but we’ve got to be better than that on offense. There’s no way around it. The three main issues in that football game were our inability to run the ball… our inability to score touchdowns in the red zone, and we’re minus-one in the turnover battle… the offense is definitely not performing as well as the defense,” he said, per FOX College Football on X, formerly Twitter. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) This week, Michigan trotted out Tommy Carr as their starting quarterback after benching Bryce Underwood last week against Penn State, but it was a predictably bad result despite the move, as Carr finished with an interception and no touchdowns on the afternoon. Michigan has proven that it is capable of hanging in there with just about anyone this season, but they are also capable of losing to anyone thanks in large part to the ineptitude of the offense, which has been an issue for the Wolverines for the last couple of years, regardless of the head coach and quarterback. Michigan will next hit the field on October 31 against Rutgers. Related: TCU fires coach after West Virginia loss, but it’s not Sonny Dykes Related: Oregon football fires offensive coordinator after another dismal performance vs. Illinois

item.title: Auction table for MI, playing for CSK franchise and back to coaching MI: Kieron Pollard's wild schedule till IPL 2027
item.description: Auction table for MI, playing for CSK franchise and back to coaching MI: Kieron Pollard's wild schedule till IPL 2027 originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Kieron Pollard will represent Mumbai Indians at the IPL 2027 mini-auction in December and will then play for a CSK franchise in January. Pollard was signed by Joburg Super Kings at the SA20 auction for R1.5 million. IPL 2027 begins in March, when Pollard is due back in the MI dugout. Kieron Pollard's next six months take him from the MI auction table to Super Kings' yellow shirt and back Nine days ago, Kieron Pollard was Mumbai Indians' batting coach who happened to have been bought by a Chennai Super Kings franchise. On Saturday, he became Mumbai Indians' head coach in the Indian Premier League, who happens to have been bought by a Chennai Super Kings franchise, and the calendar has started to look awkward. Joburg Super Kings picked him up at the SA20 mini auction on October 7 for R1.5 million, with MI Cape Town declining to bid after releasing him. It ended a decade in which Pollard had played or coached for the MI group in every league he turned up in, from MI Emirates in the ILT20 to MI New York in the MLC and MI London in The Hundred. That was already a strange enough arrangement when he was a batting coach. Now he is the man in charge of the franchise, and the dates sit on top of each other. The IPL 2027 retention deadline falls in mid-November, the mini auction is in Goa on December 16, and SA20 starts on January 17, with the final in Cape Town on February 21. One supporter did the arithmetic in public and reached the obvious conclusion. "No way, this dude gonna sit at the auction table in December for MI, then play for JSK in January-February and then Coach MI from March. The chances of Pollard pulling out of SA20 is very very high," they wrote . What a match what a knock from Tilak Varma and Nitish Kumar Reddy's knock was special too also special thanks to Naman dhir well done team India. — Kevin (@imkevin149) October 24, 2026 MORE: Kieron Pollard named as Mumbai Indians' head coach for IPL 2027 Kieron Pollard's schedule from November 2026 to August 2027 Period Commitment Team Role Mid-November 2026 IPL 2027 retention deadline Mumbai Indians Head coach December 16, 2026 IPL 2027 mini auction, Goa Mumbai Indians Head coach January 17 - February 21, 2027 SA20 Joburg Super Kings Player March - May 2027 IPL 2027 Mumbai Indians Head coach June - July 2027 Major League Cricket MI New York Player August 2027 The Hundred MI London Head coach The SA20 window is the one that does not fit. Everything else on that list belongs to the MI group, so a head coach shuttling between them is unusual but not contradictory. Spending five weeks in Super Kings yellow between the MI auction and the MI season is a different matter. Albie Morkel, the Joburg head coach who signed him, was open about what the deal was worth beyond the runs.
item.content:encoded: Auction table for MI, playing for CSK franchise and back to coaching MI: Kieron Pollard's wild schedule till IPL 2027 originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Kieron Pollard will represent Mumbai Indians at the IPL 2027 mini-auction in December and will then play for a CSK franchise in January. Pollard was signed by Joburg Super Kings at the SA20 auction for R1.5 million. IPL 2027 begins in March, when Pollard is due back in the MI dugout. Kieron Pollard's next six months take him from the MI auction table to Super Kings' yellow shirt and back Nine days ago, Kieron Pollard was Mumbai Indians' batting coach who happened to have been bought by a Chennai Super Kings franchise. On Saturday, he became Mumbai Indians' head coach in the Indian Premier League, who happens to have been bought by a Chennai Super Kings franchise, and the calendar has started to look awkward. Joburg Super Kings picked him up at the SA20 mini auction on October 7 for R1.5 million, with MI Cape Town declining to bid after releasing him. It ended a decade in which Pollard had played or coached for the MI group in every league he turned up in, from MI Emirates in the ILT20 to MI New York in the MLC and MI London in The Hundred. That was already a strange enough arrangement when he was a batting coach. Now he is the man in charge of the franchise, and the dates sit on top of each other. The IPL 2027 retention deadline falls in mid-November, the mini auction is in Goa on December 16, and SA20 starts on January 17, with the final in Cape Town on February 21. One supporter did the arithmetic in public and reached the obvious conclusion. "No way, this dude gonna sit at the auction table in December for MI, then play for JSK in January-February and then Coach MI from March. The chances of Pollard pulling out of SA20 is very very high," they wrote . What a match what a knock from Tilak Varma and Nitish Kumar Reddy's knock was special too also special thanks to Naman dhir well done team India. — Kevin (@imkevin149) October 24, 2026 MORE: Kieron Pollard named as Mumbai Indians' head coach for IPL 2027 Kieron Pollard's schedule from November 2026 to August 2027 Period Commitment Team Role Mid-November 2026 IPL 2027 retention deadline Mumbai Indians Head coach December 16, 2026 IPL 2027 mini auction, Goa Mumbai Indians Head coach January 17 - February 21, 2027 SA20 Joburg Super Kings Player March - May 2027 IPL 2027 Mumbai Indians Head coach June - July 2027 Major League Cricket MI New York Player August 2027 The Hundred MI London Head coach The SA20 window is the one that does not fit. Everything else on that list belongs to the MI group, so a head coach shuttling between them is unusual but not contradictory. Spending five weeks in Super Kings yellow between the MI auction and the MI season is a different matter. Albie Morkel, the Joburg head coach who signed him, was open about what the deal was worth beyond the runs. He pointed to what Pollard offers the franchise's under-23 group, naming Jason Rowles, and acknowledged that MI supporters would not enjoy watching it. MORE: 'Bring that energy and spirit': New MI coach Kieron Pollard warns Wankhede fans against cheering for RCB and CSK during IPL 2027 campaign Something on this list has to go, and SA20 is the obvious one Pollard has never shown much interest in slowing down. He is 39, retired from international cricket in 2022, and has spent the years since collecting roles across four leagues on three continents without appearing to find it difficult. This situation is different because the conflict is not about workload. A head coach spends the weeks after an auction working out what he has bought and how the squad fits together, and Pollard would be doing that from a dressing room belonging to the franchise MI has spent eighteen years defining themselves against. Joburg paid R1.5 million for him, which, in the context of what he earns elsewhere, is not the number that decides his year. The MI job is. Mumbai finished ninth in 2026 with four wins from 14, and a new coach walking into that does not need to spend five weeks away in January explaining why he is wearing yellow. The fan is probably right. Pollard has not said anything about pulling out, and he may yet find a way to do both, but of everything on that calendar, the SA20 stint is the one that costs him least to drop and most to keep. Pollard resolves the clash by pulling out of SA20 The schedule problem has already been settled at one end. A day after being confirmed as Mumbai Indians head coach, Pollard told Joburg Super Kings he will not be available for the 2027 SA20 season, removing the fixture overlap before it became an issue. Kasi Viswanathan, chief executive of CSK and the wider Super Kings group, confirmed the decision to Cricbuzz. "He has conveyed to us that he will not be able to play for Joburg Super Kings," he said. "We will now look for a replacement." It also tidies up an awkward arrangement that had nothing to do with dates. JSK are the Super Kings franchise in a league where the Mumbai Indians already own MI Cape Town, which passed on Pollard at the auction and bought Shimron Hetmyer instead. MI had raised no objection to him playing for a rival, with a source saying the call was his alone, but a newly appointed MI head coach turning out for a CSK-owned side was never going to sit comfortably for long. To keep up to date with all the latest cricket news and share your opinion on the biggest topics, visit our Facebook , Instagram and X (Twitter) pages.

item.title: JJ Watt doesn't understand Boye Mafe Bengals-Ravens penalty
item.description: CBS color analyst JJ Watt strongly disagreed with a personal-foul call against Cincinnati Bengals defensive lineman Boye Mafe during the second quarter of their NFL Week 7 game against the Baltimore Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium. "Mafe is flagged for that one ," play-by-play announcer Jim Nantz said during the broadcast. "That's big as they were about to get the Ravens off the field." "This is really interesting: Mafe gets cut by Derrick Henry," Watt said. "What's he supposed to do to avoid that? He got cut, and he's falling down." "As a defensive player myself, I honestly do not know what you expect me to do in that situation," Watt added. "(Bengals head coach Zac Taylor) is calling a timeout now," Nantz said. "He is irate over that call." "If that block causes him to go into that offensive player, that would absolve him," rules analyst Gene Steratore said. "When he's standing and then he lunges like that, he's going low on his own." "I get the letter of the law," Watt said. "He gets cut block by the other guy. He gets tripped. … I'm sorry, that's very difficult (for me to understand)." This article originally appeared on Cincinnati Enquirer: JJ Watt doesn't understand Boye Mafe Bengals-Ravens penalty

item.description: College football rankings: Updated NCAA Top 25 Polls after BYU, Ole Miss, Texas Tech, Tennessee losses in Week 8 originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . College football's Week 8 was not as chaotic as last week's wild slate of games, but there were plenty of surprises and upsets. Friday night gave us our first major coach firing in the FBS, as NC State fired longtime head coach Dave Doeren on Saturday after the Wolfpack fell 31-28 on the road to Stanford. Here's Bill Bender on the top candidates to replace him . In the early slate on Saturday, Indiana got gritty to survive in overtime against Michigan on the road, and Miami steamrolled past Pitt 52-23 as Canes receiver Malachi Toney had himself a monster game . The Big 12 also had a poor day , as top-ranked teams in BYU and Texas Tech lost to UCF and Cincinnati, respectively. BYU's overtime loss to the Knights was wild, as a questionable roughing the kicker penalty helped UCF pull the upset. USC dropped its second loss of the season, falling 24-7 to an unranked Wisconsin on the road. Tennessee also went down on the road, losing 27-24 to South Carolina. Also in the SEC, Texas and Arch Manning barely held off a furious second-half rally from Trinidad Chambliss and Ole Miss, winning 34-27. Now, there are a whopping seven two-loss teams inside the SEC that can all make cases for the CFP as the season reaches its back stretch. Now that Week 8 is in the books, let's take a look at where things stand with the latest rankings. MORE: Why is Pat McAfee beefing with the Utah fan base? item.title: Digging Deeper Into Liverpool’s 2-0 Victory Over Brighton
item.description: LIVERPOOL, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 25: Ronald Araujo of Liverpool celebrates after the Premier League 2026/27 match between Liverpool FC and Brighton & Hove Albion at Anfield on October 25, 2026 in Liverpool, England. (Photo by Jan Kruger/Getty Images) | Getty Images Liverpool did what was needed against a high-flying Brighton and they did it with real attacking flair in the first-half and a gritty second 45 minutes earning the Reds first win at Anfield in the Premier League this season. The swirling wind played it’s part when the ball was in the air but the core influence was Liverpool’s commitment to the cause with some determined and quality performances. Winners and Losers It’s hard to be too critical of any of the Reds, not that it was perfect because we could have scored more and did give up some opportunities for Brighton but it was a well earned win with a clean sheet to sweeten the points gained. It’s worth remembering that Brighton hadn’t conceded a goal for 548 minutes as well a staggering +18 goal difference. Let’s dig in and offer up the winners and losers. Winners: Ronald Araujo or Big Ron, after celebrating his second goal for Liverpool midweek with the fans he put in a performance that got the Kop singing his name and that’s the highest approval (especially for a loanee). Big Ron got himself another assist (technically his cross came off a Brighton player to Wirtz) through pure determination, class and passion he plays every moment with but he also blocked and tackled until the final whistle in such a manner it got Anfield on their feet roaring and chanting his name. Florian Wirtz gets a mention for putting in the type of performance that is becoming increasingly normal which should keep the noise from getting any louder about his price tag and the expectations that come with it. His name might not be put alongside Liverpool’s first goal but Wirtz still made it happen with the effort on goal but he also played some wonderful passes and was a key figure in most of the attacking flair that the Reds showed in the first-half. Bradley Barcola proved he is more than just a speed merchant down the wings with a very impressive defensive display that had Brighton trying to mostly attack down Liverpool’s left flank where Cody Gakpo and Milos Kerkez were. That’s not a criticism of either player as such but with Barcola and Araujo locking down the right side it was an obvious choice by the Brighton team. Added to Barcola’s defensive contributions he also got an assist for Liverpool’s second where he showed his pace and played in the perfect cross for Alexander Isak to put away effortlessly (thanks to his rediscovered killer instinct when around the goal). Losers: There were no real losers even if the Ref made some decisions that seemed to favor Brighton and apart from that this writer could point to all noise around Liverpool’s expensive signings not delivering enough. Winners and Losers It’s hard to be too critical of any of the Reds, not that it was perfect because we could have scored more and did give up some opportunities for Brighton but it was a well earned win with a clean sheet to sweeten the points gained. It’s worth remembering that Brighton hadn’t conceded a goal for 548 minutes as well a staggering +18 goal difference. Let’s dig in and offer up the winners and losers. Winners: Ronald Araujo or Big Ron, after celebrating his second goal for Liverpool midweek with the fans he put in a performance that got the Kop singing his name and that’s the highest approval (especially for a loanee). Big Ron got himself another assist (technically his cross came off a Brighton player to Wirtz) through pure determination, class and passion he plays every moment with but he also blocked and tackled until the final whistle in such a manner it got Anfield on their feet roaring and chanting his name. Florian Wirtz gets a mention for putting in the type of performance that is becoming increasingly normal which should keep the noise from getting any louder about his price tag and the expectations that come with it. His name might not be put alongside Liverpool’s first goal but Wirtz still made it happen with the effort on goal but he also played some wonderful passes and was a key figure in most of the attacking flair that the Reds showed in the first-half. Bradley Barcola proved he is more than just a speed merchant down the wings with a very impressive defensive display that had Brighton trying to mostly attack down Liverpool’s left flank where Cody Gakpo and Milos Kerkez were. That’s not a criticism of either player as such but with Barcola and Araujo locking down the right side it was an obvious choice by the Brighton team. Added to Barcola’s defensive contributions he also got an assist for Liverpool’s second where he showed his pace and played in the perfect cross for Alexander Isak to put away effortlessly (thanks to his rediscovered killer instinct when around the goal). Losers: There were no real losers even if the Ref made some decisions that seemed to favor Brighton and apart from that this writer could point to all noise around Liverpool’s expensive signings not delivering enough. It’s fair to say that the first-half flow of the attacking unit was very soothing to the eyes and there were at least a couple of great opportunities that should have been put away. Wirtz taking a knock to his ankle which caused him to leave the game wasn’t ideal and with the next game coming up on Wednesday it seems unlikely he will be available. Added to that was Trey Nyoni limping after a brave challenge in our penalty area and it’s going to leave us all anxious to find out the extend of either injury. Talking Tactics Andoni Iraola’s love for full energy play and aggressive press was there for all to witness as the Reds hunted down the ball in packs and was a clear sign that the nuances of a team effort are becoming like muscle memory. As mentioned with Barcola there was the tactical choice made by Brighton to attack the flank that was obviously the one felt to be the Reds weakest yet thankfully those efforts didn’t bare fruit and the clean sheet was ours. Dissecting the Narrative Liverpool hadn’t managed a win at Anfield in the Premier League thus far this season and their opponents hadn’t conceded a goal for a very long time whilst scoring plenty of goals themselves. Despite the positive gains since the loss to 114 City at Anfield there was still some nerves amongst supporters and pundits which speaks of there still being the need for the Reds to play in a way that earns complete trust in them to show up fully switched on. Today’s game could be a turning point in that trust as every player showed up and collectively they held their own to earn a tough win and clean sheet. What Happens Next Now that Liverpool are sitting in fourth spot just one point behind Brighton they have to gather themselves for a cup clash with Chelsea, minus Cole Palmer due to his suspension, at Anfield. With all the Reds anxiously waiting for news on Flo and Trey as well Dominik Szoboszlai there could be some rotation required and even possibly a chance for Wataru Endo to play. It also has to be noted that the following game is against Arsenal at Anfield so this is a big push needed by the players which may require some fresh legs and will definitely need big performances individually and collectively. Things are certainly clicking though and the belief is growing. YNWA.

item.title: Jaguars rumors: Brian Thomas Jr. trade feels inevitable, but there’s just 1 issue right now
item.description: Corey Perrine/Florida Times-Union / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images Jaguars rumors: Brian Thomas Jr. trade feels inevitable, but there’s just 1 issue right now appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Jacksonville Jaguars look to be in complete control of the AFC South. Jacksonville lost a heartbreaker in Week 6 but they are still in command of their division at 4-2. The Jaguars will be an interesting team to watch at the trade deadline, even if they don’t move one of their offensive weapons. NFL insiders Ian Rapoport and Adam Schefter shared intel from around the league in a recent article. They talked about multiple trade candidates before the deadline on November 10th. There is one snag in all of the trade rumors surrounding Jaguars receiver Brian Thomas Jr. — Jacksonville isn’t interested. “The mercurial Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver is a first-round talent who is now in his second season as the subject of trade rumors,” Rapoport and Schefter wrote. “Jacksonville has shown no signs of engaging in trade talks, though teams are expected to ramp up calls closer to the deadline. Thomas didn’t play in the second half last week against the Houston Texans, furthering speculation.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Thomas has had an unbelievable fall from grace over the past few seasons. He was incredible as a rookie, logging 87 receptions for 1,282 receiving yards and 10 touchdowns. However, everything changed once Liam Coen came to town for the 2025 season. Now BTJ is an afterthought in Jacksonville’s offense. The third-year receiver only has nine receptions for 105 receiving yards and a touchdown this year on 19 targets. It is surprising to hear that the Jaguars are not interested in trading Thomas. He does not appear to be a part of the long-term plan in Jacksonville, so getting some value from him would be wise. Perhaps Jacksonville will adjust their strategy if they receive a lucrative offer on Thomas. But at this point, it is safe to assume BTJ isn’t going anywhere. The Jaguars are on their bye in Week 7. They have extra time to prepare for a Week 8 contest against the Colts. Related: Key Trevor Lawrence protector gets brutal injury update amid Jaguars’ bye week

item.title: Is Barcelona v Real Madrid on TV? How to watch El Clasico in the UK
item.description: Barcelona and Real Madrid resume their bitter rivalry with the first El Clasico of this LaLiga campaign. Hansi Flick ’s side have the upper hand in the top flight so far, with a perfect run of nine wins from nine, while Jose Mourinho ’s visitors sit third, six points off top spot having won seven and lost two. LIVE: Barcelona vs Real Madrid: La Liga title rivals clash in first Clasico of season Barca ran out 5-2 winners in an entertaining clash with 10-man Real Betis last time out, with Lamine Yamal , Rodri and Dani Olmo all on the scoresheet, while Kylian Mbappe scored twice as Real beat Sevilla 4-1. Whatever happens it is likely to be a dramatic, all-out-attacking game: Barcelona lost 4-2 to holders PSG in a Champions League thriller on Tuesday while Madrid put four past RB Leipzig, who scored a late consolation goal, on Wednesday night. Here’s everything you need to know. When is Barcelona v Real Madrid? Barcelona host Real Madrid at Camp Nou on Sunday 25 October, with kick-off at 8pm BST. How can I watch it? Viewers in the UK can watch the game on Premier Sports 1. Team news Barcelona’s Dani Olmo picked up an injury in the defeat to PSG and joins Eric Garcia and Jules Kounde on the sidelines. Real Madrid will be without the suspended Vinicius Jr after he was sent off against Villareal and handed a four-game ban for violent conduct following a hair-pull on Nathan Saliba. The visitors will also be missing injured defender Raul Asencio. Predicted line-ups Barcelona XI: Joan Garcia, Espart, Martin, Pau Cubarsi, Cancelo, Pedri, Rodri, Adeyemi, Lopez, Yamal, Gabriel Jesus Real Madrid XI: Courtois, Cucurella, Huijsen, Konate, Valverde, Tchouameni, Guler, Diomande, Bellingham, Endrick, Mbappe

Nevertheless, Sassuolo have had their exploits this season, especially at home, where they beat Torino and their more famous neighbours, Juventus, in a dramatic 3-2 clash. Moreover, they forced AC Milan to settle for a 1-1 draw. The only team that managed to survive Gennaro Gattuso’s juggernaut was his former club AC Milan, thanks to a second-half comeback that earned them a 2-2 draw. Therefore, the Aquile currently sit at the top of the table with 22 points from a possible 24, only behind Inter Milan, who have a superior goal difference. item.title: Steelers Just Did Something No NFL Team Has Done in 4 Years
item.description: Steelers Just Did Something No NFL Team Has Done in 4 Years originally appeared on SportsNet Pittsburgh . Add SportsNet Pittsburgh as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Steelers dominated on all fronts when facing the Saints in Paris. Jaylen Warren ran for 101 yards, while Aaron Rodgers made history. He wasn’t the only one. The Saints' Tyler Shough was intercepted and got sacked twice. Pittsburgh’s defense had 67 tackles. New Orleans’ receiving core earned some solid yardage. What the defense did against New Orleans’ running game was impressive. Per ESPN Insights , the Saints only averaged 1.06 yards per rush. The team had 18 rushing yards. The leader in rushing? Shough, the QB, with seven. The Steelers entered the game ranked 14th in the fewest rushing yards allowed. The team showcased their value by forcing a fumble when Shough ran the ball. Pittsburgh won the game 16-10. With the loss, New Orleans became the first team since the Buccaneers in Week 4 of the 2022 season without a 10-yard rusher in a game. Returning to the U.S. next week, the Steelers’ defense aims to build on this game. They take on the Browns, ranked near the bottom in rushing yards per game. item.title: Barcelona expected to send a star-studded delegation to Ballon d’Or ceremony – report
item.description: Barcelona expected to send a star-studded delegation to Ballon d’Or ceremony – report Although Barcelona’s primary objective this week will be to dismantle Real Madrid in the season’s first El Clasico , the Catalans have good reasons to be even more excited about Monday’s Ballon d’Or ceremony. Ahead of the gala in London, many are expecting Barcelona to dominate proceedings, with Lamine Yamal widely tipped as the favourite to secure the Ballon d’Or trophy, ahead of Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappe and Rodri. Barcelona are also in line to win other accolades in the event, which is why we could see a large delegation in London. Barcelona’s heavy presence in Ballon d’Or ceremony Yamal will fly separately to London. (Photo by Burak Kara/Getty Images) As reported by Diario SPORT , Barcelona will deploy a sizeable representation in London for the 70th edition of the Ballon d’Or Gala, led by president Joan Laporta. The expedition will travel together to the English capital alongside all of the club’s nominees across the various award categories. On the playing side, the list includes Lamine Yamal, Pau Cubarsi, Rodri, Joan Garcia and a strong contingent from the women’s team, featuring Cata Coll, Esmee Brugts, Patri Guijarro, Caroline Graham Hansen, Claudia Pina, Ewa Pajor, Clara Serrajordi and coach Pere Romeu. On the institutional front, Laporta will be joined by vice-presidents Rafa Yuste and Elena Fort, directors Xavi Puig and Xavier Barniol, and sporting figures including Deco and Bojan Krkic. Lamine, meanwhile, will make the trip separately, having chartered a private jet for his parents, partner, family, friends and members of his team. An entertaining night in London Thierry Henry will co-host the Ballon d’Or event. (Photo by Xavi Torrent/Getty Images for Spotify) This year’s gala carries added significance, as it will be staged outside Paris for the very first time. Organisers have chosen the British capital to honour Stanley Matthews, winner of the inaugural Ballon d’Or in 1956. The London Palladium Theatre will host the event, which begins at 9pm Spanish time and is expected to conclude at around 11pm. The ceremony will be fronted by two familiar faces in former Barcelona forward Thierry Henry and British journalist Kate Scott, both of whom feature on CBS’ Champions League coverage. Organisers are also promising a show full of surprises and musical performances, with British singer Jorja Smith opening proceedings with ‘Blue Lights’ before a performance from rapper French Montana. Needless to say, it promises to be a memorable evening for Barça.

item.title: ‘Kellen Moore Is Not the Answer,’ ‘So in Over His Head’ — Calls Mount for Saints To ‘Fire’ HC After 16–10 Loss to Steelers
item.description: ‘Kellen Moore Is Not the Answer,’ ‘So in Over His Head’ — Calls Mount for Saints To ‘Fire’ HC After 16–10 Loss to Steelers When many made their predictions entering the 2026 NFL Season, the New Orleans Saints were a popular breakout pick. They finished last season strong, had one of the best drafts in 2025, and had a quarterback in Tyler Shough who elevated the offense to another level. But this is far from what has happened this season so far. The Saints were 2-4 entering the NFL’s first game in France, and when they needed to win, they fell short in an embarrassing fashion. It may be the nail in the coffin for head coach Kellen Moore. Kellen Moore’s Performance in the New Orleans Saints’ Loss Draws Criticism After hiring Moore in 2025, the expectation was that year 1 would be a free season and that improvements would come in year 2. Instead, Moore hasn’t been able to fix many issues, including the offensive line, run game, questionable personnel decisions, and needed changes that haven’t been made. He completely turned around the Saints’ red-zone success, but against the Pittsburgh Steelers this week, they even regressed in that area. In the run game this season, the Saints are ranked 25th overall per PFN’s Offensive Impact Metric . The Saints have also suffered some embarrassing games this season, which has put pressure on Owner Gayle Benson to demand better. This dude is so in over his head.” Billiot Jr. then spoke about one of the last plays of the game, where the Saints were called offsides and gave the Steelers a first down to run out the clock, “#Saints special teams player jumps offsides to cost the game, walks to the sideline, and what’s waiting for him… Kellen Moore standing there looking like a mom that’s perpetually bothered by the service at a restaurant. No emotion, no fight, no fire.” PREDIC

They finished last season strong, had one of the best drafts in 2025, and had a quarterback in Tyler Shough who elevated the offense to another level. But this is far from what has happened this season so far. The Saints were 2-4 entering the NFL’s first game in France, and when they needed to win, they fell short in an embarrassing fashion. It may be the nail in the coffin for head coach Kellen Moore. Kellen Moore’s Performance in the New Orleans Saints’ Loss Draws Criticism After hiring Moore in 2025, the expectation was that year 1 would be a free season and that improvements would come in year 2. He has no type of physicality and his team embodies that.” Saints reporter Katherine Terrell posted a comment from Moore before the game after being asked about stopping Steelers RB Jaylen Warren, and he responded with arguably the most obvious answer ever, “Kellen Moore was asked just now how they stop Jaylen Warren. This dude is so in over his head.” Billiot Jr. then spoke about one of the last plays of the game, where the Saints were called offsides and gave the Steelers a first down to run out the clock, “#Saints special teams player jumps offsides to cost the game, walks to the sideline, and what’s waiting for him… Kellen Moore standing there looking like a mom that’s perpetually bothered by the service at a restaurant. It keeps showing up. He’s not the answer.” Fantasy football writer Ryan McDowell believes that if Moore is fired, he will quickly become an offensive coordinator somewhere else, “Kellen Moore is going to be a great OC for some team next year.” One Saints fan called Moore a “substitute teacher” and expressed their interest in New Orleans hiring former Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin, “Fire Kellen Moore. The substitute teacher has to go… Run me Mike Tomlin”. Clearly, many have turned on Moore, and after the Owner’s comments just a couple of weeks ago, a change could be made soon. The Saints have been a patient team, so that may not happen until after the season, but the writing is on the wall for Moore. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

item.title: Athletic Club star confirms he rejected Barcelona & Arsenal
item.description: Athletic Club star confirms he rejected Barcelona & Arsenal Athletic Club star Nico Williams has this weekend revealed that he knocked back the interest of two of European football’s leading clubs, to stay put in Bilbao. Wide-man Nico has for his part of course long been tipped for a potential Athletic departure. After emerging as a key player for Luis de La Fuente’s Spanish national team, the 24-year-old’s talents began to be recognised beyond the confines of La Liga, throughout the continent. Back in the summer of 2025, it was Hansi Flick’s Barcelona who pushed hardest for his signature, only for Nico to surprise the masses in penning a new long-term contract at San Mamés. And speaking during an exchange with the media after playing his part in a 4-0 drubbing of Getafe on Sunday, the Spaniard confirmed that Barca were not the only high-profile suitor whom he chose to knock back. As cited by El Chiringuito TV, Nico admitted: “Apart from Barca, I had offers from PSG and Arsenal, and I rejected them. I am where I want to be. The decisions are made at home with my parents and my brother.” Conor Laird – GSFN

item.title: Arteta compiles images of Premier League managers leaving their technical area
item.description: Arteta compiles images of Premier League managers leaving their technical area Mikel Arteta has suggested he’s compiling footage of other Premier League managers after being targeted by the media and officials for leaving his technical area. Photo by Richard Heathcote/Getty Images Mikel Arteta received a booking for leaving his technical area during Arsenal’s win over Everton on Saturday, but the Gunners boss suggested afterwards that he’s far from the only one to do it. According to Arteta, some Premier League managers leave the technical area as often as 36 times in the space of 10 minutes, and he’s putting together a compilation of the offences. Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images “I do have to be careful, put sensors there [on the edge of the technical area]!” Arteta said . “There are managers that have the record in the league, 36 times in 10 minutes they leave the touchline, no yellows. “I’m clipping all of that, I have a massive storage of images, I don’t have the record yet. “Let’s see – then it’s 36 yellow cards in 10 minutes for managers, where are we going to be then? Let’s see.” Photo by Stu Forster/Getty Images There’s been a bit of an unfair focus on Arteta leaving his technical area during recent weeks and months, considering it’s such a common thing throughout the Premier League. As one of the division’s top teams and current champions, perhaps it’s to be expected that Arsenal would be the team the league use to make an example for the other managers. But that’s hardly fair on the Gunners, giving them a different rulebook to the rest of the league. The occasional yellow card here or there shouldn’t do too much to Arsenal’s Premier League title chances. But if it starts leading to suspensions, and the Gunners have to play matches without their manager for the same offence that’s going unpunished elsewhere, then that’s a problem. With any luck, Arteta bringing his compilation of images to the Premier League will lead to a fairer application of the punishment across all 20 teams. Photo by Shaun Botterill/Getty Images

item.content:encoded: In this episode of Motley Fool Rule Breaker Investing , Motley Fool co-founder David Gardner talks with Kimball Crossley, longtime sports journalist, coach, and baseball scout, about taking a fresh look at America's favorite sport. To catch full episodes of all The Motley Fool's free podcasts, check out our podcast center . When you're ready to invest, check out this top 10 list of stocks to buy . Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue » A full transcript is below. Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. If you’d invested $5,000 then, you’d be sitting on $2,742,263 today.* Now, for the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. It’s a key player in the $1.8 trillion space race, and with the stock recently sitting 20% off its highs, the window to get in early is closing fast. Continue » *Stock Advisor returns as of October 25, 2026. This podcast was recorded on Oct. 14, 2026. David Gardner: It's that time of year again. America's most popular sport is in full swing, both at the NFL professional level and, of course, the college professional level as well. Football dominates our weekends, our conversations for millions of us, our fantasy leagues. Every week we watch referees throw flags. Coaches make decisions, and fans argue about rules that perhaps nobody had previously thought to question. Well, this week, we're questioning them. My friend Kimball Crossley returns to challenge some of football's sacred cows. Help us rethink a few rules, maybe. Remind us that even America's favorite game has plenty of room for rulebreakers, breaking the rules of sports volume two, American football only on this week's Rule Breaker Investing . When Kimball Crossley first joined me back in April 2025 for breaking the rules of sports, I invited him to do what rule Breakers love doing, and that's challenge conventional wisdom. Kimball came ready to play. He brought three provocative assertions. First was that momentum in sports is largely a fiction. We love talking about it, and we're not very good at proving it exists. Second, that quarterback is the most overrated position in sports. Well, the most important position in football certainly also the most overrated. Third, that basketball should eliminate the corner three-point shot, which Kimball argued has helped make the modern game increasingly predictable and homogeneous. We're not going to talk about those this time because that's what we did last time. But if you're a sports fan, I think you're going to enjoy that April 2025 podcast. This one is breaking the rules of sports volume two. It's football season. A lot of people are talking and thinking about football, and that's what we're doing on this week's podcast, as well. Yes, my return guest this week is my longtime friend Kimball Crossley, a sports journalist, podcaster, high school basketball coach, who's also worked as a Major League baseball scout since 1999, most recently, the San Diego Padres now in his ninth season. For years, Kimball hosted Three Point Range. That's a podcast devoted to challenging conventional wisdom. In sports, he continues to blog from Substack at Three Point Range. If you find yourself interested in our conversation this week, especially if you're a college basketball fan, he's going deep into the Xs and Os of the college game on Three Point Range on Substack. But Kimball spent decades thinking critically about the games we love. I'm also happy to say both he and I attended the same New England high school where we happen to both have played varsity football. Kimball, as it turns out, you didn't have enough, nor did I to play football at our alma mater, the University of North Carolina. Did you walk on? Kimball Crossley: No, I didn't, not after my horrible high school record. David Gardner: Well, before we get into football, our topic this week, I do want to acknowledge something, and that's that not everybody listening to this week's podcast is a sports fan. Even among those who are, I don't know, American football, it may not be your game. That's perfectly fine. One of the things I've always loved about Rule Breaker thinking is that it travels well, whether we're talking about investing, business, life or sports. Here's what I'd like to do. Kimball, you've come prepared today with some provocative ideas about how to make American football better. But before we get into those specifics, I want you to give us a broader lesson. Think, especially of people who don't care about sports and tuned into this week's podcast. Right up front, Kimball, if you were to abstract what we're really doing this week and then we'll let all the non-sports fans go, what at the heart underlies these things we're going to be talking about about football? Kimball Crossley: Well, I think it's quite simply the punishment needs to fit the crime, and that probably goes for just about anything in our society. Certainly, I think it's necessary in sports. It undermines sports if it doesn't. As much as I love the NFL, I think there's several areas, a few of them we'll talk about today, where there's no question in my mind that punishment doesn't fit the crime, and it drives me crazy when I watch a game, and I expect that's a lot of our listeners, as well. David Gardner: Excellent. A lot of us are used to in the short term, the stock market, as has often said Warren Buffett, Charlie Munger, et cetera, in the long term, the stock market is a weighing machine, but in the short term, the stock market is a voting machine. In some ways, I think investors can sympathize with what you've just said, Kimball, because in the short term, stocks can be misunderstood and mispriced. The punishment or the reward may not fit the action or the value of the thing itself. But in the long term, at least in the stock market, I think it's a weighing machine, and I think over the long term, you should be getting the just desserts for better or for worse based on the investment you've made. Now, let me just say, there you go, fools, for the rest of our time together, Kimball and I are going to be bringing ideas to life about American football. If that's your sport, you're in for a treat. If it isn't, you've already got your primary rule-breaker thought to take with you today. Thanks for joining us, and we'll hope to see you again next week. Kimball, let's get into it now. I think you have three provocations. I don't know if that's the right word or not, but three things that you think, if we fix them, football would be a better game. Let's get started with number one. What is it? Kimball Crossley: Well, definitely, the NFL would be better. I know some of these rules, well, at least one of them is different in college, and I'll start with that one, the pass interference rule, which drives me crazy in the NFL. I guess a couple of reasons that drives me crazy is it's probably one of the harder things to call. It's not something that can be is reviewable. Yet, it's the most damaging to a team if it's called on them. It is just, if you think about it, often the penalty is 30, 40 yards for a hand on his shoulder, or maybe he touched him, or maybe he didn't. But actually, the offensive player created the contact. What's up with that? It's worth three or four holding penalties for just one pass interference. It's always driven me crazy, especially a couple of factors figure in. There's no question in my mind, if you're in trouble and you're facing third and 20, just chuck it long, have your receiver get tangled up with his defender, and start waving your hands up in the air and crying.

item.title: NASCAR at Talladega: What Time Is the Race? TV Schedule, Radio and Why Anyone Can Win
item.description: Oct 4, 2026; Las Vegas, Nevada, USA; Joe Gibbs Racing driver Chase Briscoe (19) during the South Point 400 at Las Vegas Motor Speedway. Mandatory Credit: Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images TALLADEGA, Ala. — Buckle up, NASCAR fans. Talladega is back, the championship fight is heating up, and somebody’s Sunday afternoon could get turned upside down in a hurry. The NASCAR Cup Series heads to Talladega Superspeedway on Sunday for the YellaWood 500. Chase Briscoe starts on the pole, Kyle Larson leads the championship standings, and nobody should feel too comfortable. At Talladega, a strong car helps. Good friends in the draft help even more. But sometimes, all it takes is one bad push to turn a championship contender into a very expensive lawn dart. NASCAR at Talladega: TV schedule and radio information Race: YellaWood 500 Date: Sunday, Oct. 25 Track: Talladega Superspeedway in Talladega, Alabama TV channel: NBC Pre-race coverage: 1:30 p.m. ET TV Race start: 2 p.m. ET Green Flag: 2:25 p.m. ET Radio: Motor Racing Network (MRN) and SiriusXM NASCAR Radio Streaming: Peacock and HBO Max Race distance: 188 laps, 500 miles Chase Briscoe earned the pole with a qualifying lap averaging 186.065 mph. Austin Hill joins him on the front row, while Trackhouse Racing teammates Connor Zilisch and Shane van Gisbergen start third and fourth. Larson starts fifth in the championship conversation but 10th on the grid. The Hendrick Motorsports driver enters with just a five-point lead over Christopher Bell, making every position potentially valuable. Penske speed, manufacturer battles and pit-road strategy Talladega is about more than horsepower. It’s about teamwork, timing and knowing when to trust the driver pushing your rear bumper at nearly 200 mph. Team Penske’s Ford camp will be worth watching, with Ryan Blaney and Austin Cindric starting 27th and 28th. Those starting spots mean work awaits, but superspeedway racing offers plenty of opportunities to charge forward. The Ford, Chevrolet and Toyota camps will spend the afternoon battling for drafting partners and control of the lanes. Manufacturer alliances can create powerful runs, but those partnerships can change quickly when the checkered flag gets closer. Then there’s the beauty of green-flag pit stops. When the field dives onto pit road under green, crews must execute flawlessly while drivers and teams calculate whether to stop together or gamble on track position. One mistimed stop can cost a driver the draft. A perfectly timed one can put a car at the front of the field before anyone realizes what happened. And with 500 miles ahead, the strategy will keep changing. Why anyone can win at Talladega Larson may lead the standings, but Talladega doesn’t care about points totals. Briscoe has the pole, Penske has the speed, and the field is packed with drivers capable of making a winning move. Seven championship contenders entered the weekend within 56 points of Larson. With only three races remaining after this round begins
