Manufacturer alliances can create powerful runs, but those partnerships can change quickly when the checkered flag gets closer. Then there’s the beauty of green-flag pit stops. When the field dives onto pit road under green, crews must execute flawlessly while drivers and teams calculate whether to stop together or gamble on track position. One mistimed stop can cost a driver the draft. A perfectly timed one can put a car at the front of the field before anyone realizes what happened. And with 500 miles ahead, the strategy will keep changing. Why anyone can win at Talladega Larson may lead the standings, but Talladega doesn’t care about points totals. Briscoe has the pole, Penske has the speed, and the field is packed with drivers capable of making a winning move. Seven championship contenders entered the weekend within 56 points of Larson. With only three races remaining after this round begins, the stakes are enormous. The final laps could feature two-wide racing, three-wide racing and drivers making moves that look brilliant until they suddenly aren’t. One late caution could change everything. One push in the wrong place could trigger the dreaded Big One. That’s the magic of Talladega. A driver can spend 499 miles positioning himself perfectly and still need one last break to win. So grab the snacks, tune in to NBC or MRN, and prepare for a Sunday that could get wild in a hurry. At Talladega, the only safe prediction is that the finish probably won’t be boring.

item.title: Referee defends controversial decision amid Bade head injury Drama in Hoffenheim win
item.description: Referee defends controversial decision amid Bade head injury Drama in Hoffenheim win Refree Robert Hartmann has explained his decision not to immediately stop play following the frightenng head collision involving Loic Bade and Max Moerstedt during Hoffenheim's 3-0 win against Bayer Leverkusen on Sunday. The incident took place in the closing stages of the Bundesliga encounter in Sinsheim, with the two players clashing heads near the halfway line in the build-up to Alexander Prass' 89th-minute goal. Despite both players going to ground after the collision, referee Hartmann allowed play to continue, resulting in Prass doubling Hoffenheim's lead. The decision sparked frustration among the Leverkusen squad, while head coach Carles Martinez was furious. As quoted by the Kölner Stadt-Anzeiger, Hartmann said after the match: “I decided to play advantage because it was a foul by the Leverkusen player. I didn't immediately recognise the seriousness of the injury.” Alongside this, what he told DAZN revealed more. “For me, it wasn't a collision,” he said. "Rather, it was actually the case that the Leverkusen player (Bade) arrived a split second too late in the header duel, making it a foul by him. “I then decided to play advantage because there was momentum towards the goal, and the player was able to finish within a few seconds. At that point, I wasn't even fully aware of the severity of the injury. “I had no diagnosis. I'm not a doctor, but a referee, trained to assess the situation holistically. I feel totally sorry for the player,” concluded Hartmann.

item.title: Iraola happy after his first league win at Anfield as Liverpool boss
item.description: Liverpool's Alexander Isak celebrates scoring his side's second goal during the English Premier League soccer match between Liverpool and Brigtion and Hove Albion at Anfield, Liverpool. (is associated with: «Iraola happy after his first league win at Anfield as Liverpool boss») Peter Byrne/PA Wire/dpa Andoni Iraola declared himself happy after recording his first Premier League win at Anfield as Liverpool head coach by beating Brighton 2-0. Florian Wirtz’s shot deflected in off Pascal Gross for a 17th-minute own goal and less than five minutes later Alexander Isak doubled the lead as the Seagulls’ miserly defence was breached after more than nine hours without conceding. “Very happy for today, very happy overall for this fourth (league) win,” said Iraola. “I think we faced a very good opposition and I think it was key how we started today. We needed a strong start, be aggressive, recover balls, win our duels, be dangerous in transitions. “I think we’ve done that and it has been a different game from the last ones, where we’ve conceded first. “After, you need the comeback. Today we’ve started better and the game has gone differently.” Isak made it six goals in seven Premier League appearances and is starting to show why the club broke the British transfer record to bring him to the club last summer. “If we can put him in those positions, we can provide him good crosses, good situations, he will score the goals,” Iraola added. “I think it’s a matter of, in this case, Bradley (Barcola) winning the duel, going one v one, being faster than the opposition and finding good spots.” Wirtz was later forced off with an injury but Iraola is hopeful it will not be a significant issue. “Unfortunately, he had to leave the pitch with a small twist of the ankle,” he added. “It doesn’t look very big but we are playing every three days so we need to see where he is.” Brighton had 64% possession and 17 shots and although Yasin Ayari hit a post, only one effort was on target. Nevertheless, boss Fabian Hürzeler claimed his side deserved more. “I think everyone in the stadium saw that there was one team who really tried to create and try to win this game and therefore I have to praise my players,” he said. “There was a missed opportunity for us. Before they scored, we had one, two big chances and I think it was just the difference that they scored, we didn’t score. “They kept a clean sheet because they defended well. They blocked a lot of shots. They really defended the box well. We didn’t have that efficiency. “We couldn’t keep the clean sheet because we made easy mistakes, we lost some important personal duels. “But overall I saw a team with a lot of good things to take away. I saw a team that really had the belief in our approach. “That stuck to the match plan, that always kept going, and that is very frustrating because we all have the feeling that there is a missed opportunity here today.”

item.title: Gary Neville: Carrick exit ‘probably necessary’ as Man Utd ‘in mess’
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Manchester United manager Michael Carrick reacts during the English Carabao Cup third round soccer match between Manchester United and Brighton and Hove Albion at Old Trafford. (is associated with: «Gary Neville: Carrick exit ‘probably necessary’ as Man Utd ‘in mess’») Martin Rickett/PA Wire/dpa Gary Neville accepted Michael Carrick’s departure from Manchester United was “probably necessary” with the club in an “absolute mess”. United were ripped apart by Bournemouth on Sunday, with a humiliating 3-0 Old Trafford defeat coming just four days after capitulating at Como in the Champions League. Former United midfielder Carrick succeeded Ruben Amorim in January and oversaw a revival that took them to third place in the Premier League and back to the Champions League. But United have won only once in eight Premier League games this season, and are now just one point above the relegation zone in 16th place. “It’s going to get ridiculously difficult for Michael Carrick to be Manchester United manager moving forward,” former club captain Neville said in his Sky Sports commentary. “It’s horrible to say that. I played with him, I know him.” Speaking over pictures of disgruntled fans and also those showing chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox sat in the stand, Neville suggested Carrick’s departure as head coach was imminent. He said: “The Manchester United fans are singing the Michael Carrick song because I think they know what’s going to happen here. They’ve seen this before. “He’s one of their own and he’s popular. But the owners, the sporting department, and the players are not popular. “They have badly let this football club down and those two (Berrada and Wilcox) are probably going to make a decision that will disgust Manchester United fans, but is probably necessary. “It’s just an absolute mess. The football club is a mess right now.” Former United player Ashley Young criticized the players’ lack of effort and unity as their winless run stretched to eight games. “Michael Carrick is a legend of the football club, but the players on the pitch showed nothing,” Young told Sky Sports. “They didn’t go out and run, they didn’t look like a team together. If you looked at the Bournemouth team, you’d swap every single player for that Manchester United team. “You look at Ineos (United’s minority owners) and what they did over the summer. They haven’t got the players in. “But players at times have got to stand up and be counted. No togetherness, all individuals. “It’s disappointing to see Michael Carrick like that, I wish there were players there who have the love for the club he’s got. “Players might look a little bit dejected, but I think Michael knows the writing is on the wall.” Jamie Carragher urged United to change manager for Carrick’s sake. item.title: ‘There Was Not a Lot Of Warning’ — Sophie Cunningham Breaks Silence On Amber Cox, Kelly Krauskopf’s Exits During Fever’s Offseason Overhaul
item.description: Indiana Fever President of Basketball and Business Operations, Kelly Krauskopf, and Indiana Fever COO and General Manager, Amber Cox, introduced guard Sophie Cunningham to the media on Tuesday, March 11, 2025. The Indiana Fever’s season ended earlier than anyone in Indianapolis wanted. Indiana’s first-round loss to Las Vegas was followed by a major front-office shake-up, although Kelly Krauskopf had informed leadership before the regular season ended that she planned to step down. Now Fever guard Sophie Cunningham has spoken up about the changes. Sophie Cunningham’s Recent Comments Regarding the Indiana Fever Front Office Shake-Up In a recent interview with Yahoo Sports , Cunningham acknowledged that the exits of Amber Cox and Krauskopf came as a surprise, noting there was little indication beforehand that such major changes were imminent. “There was not a lot of warning, and that’s okay. I think that’s probably a good thing that you kind of keep it in-house a little bit,” Cunningham said during the interview. At the same time, the Fever guard had kind words for both of them and said she admired the work they put in. “Kelly and Amber, they’re phenomenal, phenomenal people. They cared a lot about us as players and as individuals outside the court. And so I have nothing but great things to say about them. Hopefully, the Fever come in and bring people who can do a really good job for that program. And so I was blessed to be under Kelly and Amber. And I hope that they get the very best. And so we’ll see what happens,” Cunningham added. On Friday morning, the Fever announced that longtime executive Krauskopf would step down as team president. According to the organization , Krauskopf told leadership about her decision before the 2026 regular season ended. So Krauskopf’s departure was in motion well before the playoff loss. “It has been an honor and a privilege to help build and steward the Indiana Fever with the support and trust of [owner] Herb Simon.” “I am deeply grateful for the opportunities, relationships, and shared accomplishments that have shaped my time with this organization. The Fever is poised for an exciting future, and I am proud to have helped lay the foundation for its continued growth and success,” Krauskopf said in a statement. MORE: ‘Stephanie White Is Next,’ ‘One of the Worst GMs’ – WNBA Fans React to Amber Cox’s Firing As Fever Undergo Massive Front Office Overhaul On the same day, general manager Cox was fired after two seasons with the organization. She was hired in October 2024 as chief operating officer and general manager. During her roughly two years in the job, the Fever made the playoffs both seasons. That includes a 2025 Commissioner’s Cup win and a run to Game 5 of the WNBA semifinals that year. This past season, the team also set a franchise record with 28 wins, though it went out in the first round. With Cox gone and Krauskopf stepping down, the Fever face important decisions as they prepare for the next WNBA season.

item.title: Sophie Cunningham sounds off on Indiana Fever front office changes
item.description: The Indiana Fever have dealt with a lot of drama and change over the past couple of weeks. They fired their general manager, Amber Cox. She had been with the team since 2024. She wasn’t the only one leaving. Kelly Krauskopf stepped down as president of basketball and business operations. Krauskopf had two stints with the franchise. The Fever couldn’t get out of the first round, and many criticized their offseason moves. Indiana has a couple of key free agents, including the always polarizing Sophie Cunningham . She was at F1 in Austin and weighed in on the team’s future. MORE: Indiana Fever make front-office changes after Caitlin Clark’s 3rd WNBA season What did Sophie Cunningham say about Fever’s changes? Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham (8) celebrates a made shot at Gainbridge Fieldhouse. Credit: Trevor Ruszkowski-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Sophie Cunningham is never afraid to share her opinion. That was no different when asked about the major changes within the Fever’s franchise. The 30-year-old had this to say: “There was not a lot of warning and that’s okay. I think that’s probably a good thing that you kind of keep it in-house a little bit. But you know what, Kelly and Amber, they’re phenomenal, phenomenal people. They cared a lot about us as players and as individuals outside the court, and so I have nothing but great things to say about them. Hopefully the fever come in and bring people who can do a really good job for that program and so I was blessed to be under Kelly and Amber and I hope them the very best and so we’ll see what happens” Just come across this …… pic.twitter.com/bzwasBmDAA — Lauren 🤟🏼 (@LaurenJBH1) October 25, 2026 It was interesting that she talked like she might not be back with the organization. Cunningham is a free agent, but there’s always noise around her, and it could impact her future . The Missouri product is a capable 3-and-D type player. She averaged 7.9 PPG while shooting 41.9% from three-point land. She plays well with Caitlin Clark and serves as her ‘enforcer’ when teams get physical with her. Clark could have a say in Cunningham’s future and will likely be consulted on roster decisions. item.title: College football rankings 2026: AP Top 25 poll entering Week 9
item.description: Another weekend of college football is in the books, with another wild day of upsets across the nation. Five teams ranked inside the top 16 were upset by unranked teams, including No. 2 BYU. With a wild weekend behind us, it is time to check out the latest AP Top 25 rankings . Of course, there were several shakeups following the chaotic week. MORE: Updated ESPN FPI college football top 25 rankings after upset-filled Week 8 The Miami Hurricanes continue to hold onto the top spot, earning 59 first-place votes. Ohio State checks in at No. 2, while the Georgia Bulldogs, Indiana Hoosiers, and Notre Dame round out the top five. Oct 24, 2026; Miami Gardens, Florida, USA; Miami Hurricanes quarterback Darian Mensah (10) celebrates after throwing a touchdown pass against the Pittsburgh Panthers during the fourth quarter at Hard Rock Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Where does your favorite team stand in the updated AP poll ? Below is a full look at the AP Top 25 poll following Week 8 of the 2026 season. MORE: College football stock up, stock down from Week 8: Big 12 playoff hopes take hit 2026 AP Top 25 Poll Entering Week 9 Jan 8, 2026; Glendale, AZ, USA; Miami Hurricanes cheerleaders perform during the 2026 Fiesta Bowl and semifinal game of the College Football Playoff at State Farm Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Miami (7-0 (59 first-place votes) Ohio State (6-1) (10 first-place votes) Georgia (6-1) Indiana (7-1) Notre Dame (6-1) Utah (7-0) (1 first-place vote) UCLA (7-0) BYU (6-1) Kentucky (7-1) Alabama (6-2) Texas (5-2) Ole Miss (5-2) Texas Tech (6-1) Wake Forest (6-1) LSU (6-2) Tennessee (6-2) Florida (5-2) Houston (6-2) SMU (6-1) Boise State (6-1) Northwestern (6-1) Arizona (6-1) Missouri (5-2) Oklahoma State (5-2) Wisconsin (5-2) Others receiving votes : Iowa (5-2) 76, New Mexico (6-1) 41, Cincinnati (5-2) 11, Oregon State (5-2) 11, South Carolina (4-3) 8, Minnesota (5-2) 7, USC (6-2) 7, UTSA 1, Virginia Tech (6-2) 1. The Associated Press rankings carry more weight than polls like the Coaches Poll and FWAA Poll, as they are part of the deciding factor in which teams reach the College Football Playoff. The Coaches Poll, which is not part of the College Football Playoff selection committee’s formula to determine the four teams that will compete for the College Football Playoff National Championship, is voted on by 65 FBS head coaches. The Associated Press began its college football poll on Oct. 19, 1936, and it is now the longest-running poll of those that award national titles at the end of the season. The preseason poll was started in 1950. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

The Associated Press rankings carry more weight than polls like the Coaches Poll and FWAA Poll, as they are part of the deciding factor in which teams reach the College Football Playoff. The Coaches Poll, which is not part of the College Football Playoff selection committee’s formula to determine the four teams that will compete for the College Football Playoff National Championship, is voted on by 65 FBS head coaches. The Associated Press began its college football poll on Oct. 19, 1936, and it is now the longest-running poll of those that award national titles at the end of the season. item.title: Max Verstappen delivers telling Antonelli verdict ahead of future F1 title showdown
item.description: Max Verstappen is relishing the prospect of fighting 2026's champion-elect Kimi Antonelli in next year's F1 world championship, with the Dutchman hoping to have a competitive enough car to battle the Mercedes driver. Since the return of F1 from the summer break, no driver has looked able to challenge Antonelli quite as much as Red Bull's Verstappen. The four-time champion is chasing his third straight victory at the US GP, although he lines up behind the 20-year-old pole-sitter in Sunday's Grand Prix. Antonelli starts on Pole knowing he could be 56 laps away from becoming the youngest-ever F1 world champion. Should the Italian win the race, while teammate George Russell finished P9 or lower, and Lewis Hamilton finishes lower than fifth, he will be champion. In any case, a victory for Antonelli would mathematically rule out Verstappen from becoming a five-time world champion in 2026, but the pair could not hide their excitement over a potential battle the following year. Speaking together during the post-Qualifying press conference, Antonelli began: "I think it will be amazing, of course. You know, Max is at an incredible level, and it's very tough to beat him, especially when he's got the momentum." "But yeah, it will be a lot of fun to fight as well from already now and then for the future. Of course, it will be very tough, but a good challenge. Verstappen: Antonelli a 'deserving winner' Photo: Race Pictures Photo: Race Pictures Sat next to Antonelli, Verstappen said he hoped both Mercedes and Red Bull will be able to fight for the title next year, while also commenting on the battles the pair have had so far in 2026. "Yeah, same for me, of course, Verstappen said."We are depending a little bit, hopefully, on our cars. Hopefully, they're both competitive next year as well. But yeah, from the battles that we've had so far, it's been nice. Turning his attention more closely to Antonelli's performances on the way to what will surely be his first F1 title, Verstappen praised the young Italian, adding that once officially crowned champion, he will be a "deserving winner." "And of course, this year, I think Kimi fully deserves all the success that he's having. He's very consistent, he's putting the performances in when it matters, and once it's finally official that he is World Champion, he's definitely a deserving winner."

item.title: Arch Manning lobbies Holly Rowe to cover more Texas games: ‘We’re 3-0 with you’
item.description: Credit: ESPN The Arch Manning and Holly Rowe reconciliation tour returned to Austin on Saturday night, and Manning wants it to become a weekly residency. After Texas held off Ole Miss 34-27, surviving a recovered onside kick in the closing minutes, Manning, who threw for 212 yards and ran in the go-ahead touchdown, wrapped up his on-field interview with Rowe by lobbying for a little more of the ESPN sideline reporter’s company. Just six weeks ago, Steve Sarkisian marked the occasion of Texas erasing a 20-point fourth-quarter deficit to beat Ohio State 24-23 by blowing off Rowe’s postgame interview , shouting “Texas fight” and “Hook ’em” at her before jogging off to celebrate. The snub followed a halftime interview with Laura Rutledge that Sark skipped after technical issues left him waiting, and he took plenty of heat for both. But things got more disconcerting the next day when Manning cackled with reporters about an AI-edited video showing Sarkisian slapping Rowe. What followed was as predictable as it was exhausting . Manning and Sarkisian issued their apologies, a cottage industry of online contrarians tried to recast Rowe as the villain , and Uncle Eli delivered a stern talk about trusting the media. By the time Texas squeaked past Tennessee on Sept. 26, everyone was trading warm, perfectly normal pleasantries , and the republic was saved. Which brings us to Saturday night in Austin, where Texas survived a white-knuckle finish against Ole Miss. “Whatever it takes.” Arch Manning and @TexasFootball get a BIG win over No. 7 Ole Miss https://t.co/WxPMYFtlbE — SEC Network (@SECNetwork) October 25, 2026 “You need to start doing our games more. We’re 3-0 with you this year,” Manning told Rowe. “Hey, we’ll take it,” she replied, though not before the internet spent the rest of the night forensically examining her face as she walked out of frame, trying to determine whether it was a grimace or a grin. (It may have just been a person reacting to a compliment, which is something people do.) Whether ESPN sends Rowe back to Austin for next Saturday’s game against Mississippi State is out of Manning’s hands. But after his last joke about Holly Rowe sparked a national backlash, it’s nice to see he’s finally found one she can laugh at, too. The post Arch Manning lobbies Holly Rowe to cover more Texas games: ‘We’re 3-0 with you’ appeared first on Awful Announcing .

item.title: Fernandes gamble leaves Carrick to carry the can for United’s institutional failures
item.description: Leaving out his captain was doomed to fail but so are the club under its current leadership, and the fans at Old Trafford know that all too well Dropping your captain, the man that has held the team together for most of the past five years, is a bold move from a man whose job is on the line. It was very much a make-or-break decision from Michael Carrick to leave out Bruno Fernandes against Bournemouth. It did not work, and Carrick knew the consequences if it failed and will probably pay the price for it, but he should not be alone. Carrick said the decision to drop Fernandes was purely based on football reasons but criticising his manager after the desperate defeat to Como cannot have helped. Clearly Carrick disagreed with his captain’s comments on the lack of pressing in the Champions League fixture. It was somewhat telling that Lisandro Martínez kept his place despite pointing out the director of football, Jason Wilcox, was a hindrance to the club the previous week. Continue reading...

item.title: Scottish Premiership: Durán caps Celtic’s comeback win over Hibernian
item.description: Hibernian 1-2 Celtic; Rangers 4-0 St Johnstone Braga and Miller give Hearts 2-0 win at Motherwell Camilo Durán moved into double figures for the season as Celtic reasserted themselves at the top of the Premiership by coming from behind to defeat beleaguered Hibernian 2-1 at windy Easter Road. After another Europa League setback at home to Celta Vigo on Thursday, the champions bounced back with a victory that restored their four-point cushion over Rangers at the top. The home side, who are bottom, took an early lead through Owen Elding but it was swiftly cancelled out by a Jason Kerr own goal before Duran’s 10th of the season edged the visitors ahead just before the break. Continue reading...

item.title: Osula and Barnes’ second-half burst sees Newcastle pile pressure on lacklustre Palace
item.description: The first half was one of the worst 45 minutes of football in Premier League history. The pass completion rate was a meagre 72.8%, although it felt lower. There were only two shots on target. The sun kept popping out from behind the clouds to take a look, and then going back in again, appalled. And the really bad news for Crystal Palace is that, for them, that was the good bit. Newcastle were much improved after the break. Will Osula touched in a Jacob Murphy cross two minutes after half-time, Joe Willock had an effort ruled out for a marginal offside five minutes later, and Harvey Barnes completed a slick passing move six minutes after that. A smattering of boos from the home fans made clear what everybody already knew. Quarter of an hour of proper football had been enough to win the game, and that leaves Pierre Sage under significant pressure. Continue reading...

They lack imagination, cohesion, fight, confidence and anything resembling joy, and so now hovering a point above the drop zone, survival cannot be taken for granted. Continue reading...

item.title: Isak applies finishing touch as Liverpool bring Brighton’s winning run to an end
item.description: Brighton’s impressive run was blown off course at Anfield where Liverpool performed with an appetite and urgency at both ends of the pitch that showed Andoni Iraola’s methods taking root. It was Liverpool, deserving winners on home soil for the first time in the Premier League this season, who looked upwardly mobile. There was more evidence of the expensive trio of Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Bradley Barcola feeling at home and adapting to Iraola’s demands. Wirtz was instrumental in an opening goal officially credited to Brighton’s Pascal Gross and Isak scored for the sixth time in six Premier League appearances to shatter the visitors’ sequence of four successive league wins. The sight of Barcola sprinting back to help his defence and Ronald Araújo smashing into challenges, as Liverpool stubbornly defended their lead and their box in the second half, satisfied Iraola just as much as his side’s incisiveness before the break. Continue reading...

item.title: Ballon d’Or ceremony returns to England in nod to ‘revolutionary’ Stanley Matthews
item.description: Matthews’ family ‘very excited’ as London Palladium hosts event 70 years after first award at Blackpool town hall When football’s dignitaries assemble on Monday at the London Palladium for the Ballon d’Or ceremony it will be a far cry from the first awards 70 years ago. That was held in the slightly less glamorous surroundings of Blackpool town hall, where Stanley Matthews was presented with the prize by Gabriel Hanot, the visionary editor of L’Équipe who came up with the idea of crowning the world’s best player every year. A specially commissioned china plate was also handed over by the town’s mayor before the 41-year-old Matthews, who was famously teetotal, gave a short speech. “He might have had a double carrot juice that day,” says his son, Stanley Matthews Jr, who will attend this year’s awards with his sister, Jean, and her two daughters. “There was no ceremony. ‘Here’s your Ballon d’Or, well done’, sort of thing. But obviously it’s grown over the years, and now it’s a huge event. We’re very excited.” Continue reading...

item.title: Ian Holloway’s circus: why the manager’s antics are no laughing matter for fans
item.description: Swindon manager has a history of viral outbursts but fans want a united club and manager they can support In Ian Holloway’s often madcap managerial orbit, this was simply the latest in a steady succession of eccentric outbursts. Eyes bulging as he spoke, he boomed the letter “D” and promptly stabbed himself in the chest with an imaginary dagger. Next came the letter “M” alongside a blow from another invisible knife. Finally, a “W” followed by a jab to the heart. “Dead. Man. Walking,” he declared, pausing for effect between words and briefly falling into an Oscar-worthy zombie stupor. “That’s how it feels.” To an offbeat press conference genre containing seagulls following trawlers and self-proclaimed special ones, it was a crazy new entry worthy of its subsequent viral nature. Holloway at his finest. Continue reading...

item.title: Glitch in Chelsea’s coding costs Alonso while resurgent Spurs are all systems go | Barney Ronay
item.description: Home side broke the game open with some unique corner routines, but a goalkeeping error ruined the plan There was an odd interlude at Stamford Bridge with 76 minutes gone and the score still 0-0, one of those moments where suddenly your brain seems to be on inside out, like trying to walk the wrong way down an escalator. Tottenham had a corner on the left-hand side, in a game that had felt to that point like an extended practice session, a refinement of systems, the football equivalent of watching two middle-aged men methodically emptying the dishwasher, adding salt, descaling the hoses, tutting over knives incorrectly slotted, cups in the wrong row. item.title: Tottenham stun Chelsea for second league win in a week as Cole Palmer is sent off
item.description: There are days when Tottenham go into these big games and find ways to beat themselves. This time, though, they held their nerve at a ground where they have mostly only known doom. Spurs played with control, stayed patient and won at Stamford Bridge for the first time since 2018 after waiting for Chelsea to press the self-destruct button during a calamitous and comical ending to a cagey game. Chelsea were meant to have grown. Xabi Alonso had even praised his side’s emotional control and ability to manage awkward spells during the buildup, but perhaps that was asking for trouble. Chelsea, short of poise on and off the pitch, deserved to be beaten at home for the first time this season and there was plenty of blame to go around after Alonso got his tactics wrong, Mike Penders scored a ridiculous own goal and Cole Palmer was sent off after a lunge on Conor Gallagher when he was already on a booking. Continue reading...

item.title: Championship roundup: Southampton beat West Ham; QPR put five past Swansea
item.description: Hammers humbled at home; Swansea thrashed 5-0 Burnley sack manager Hayen after 4-1 loss at Lincoln Southampton announced themselves in the promotion race with a statement 3-2 win at the pre-season title favourites, West Ham . Kuryu Matsuki, James Bree and Lewis Dobbin were all on target in a chaotic first half, while Kyle Walker-Peters and Tomas Soucek replied for the Hammers. Nuno Espírito Santo’s side would have gone top with a win but instead saw their nine-match unbeaten run halted. There were thousands of empty seats by the end at the London Stadium, with those who stayed booing the Hammers off. Southampton, deducted four points at the start of the season, are now just two points behind West Ham. Continue reading...

item.title: Maresca ‘not worried’ by Guéhi’s gaffes as Aston Villa end City’s flawless start
item.description: Defender costs three goals in past two league matches Emery praises ‘fantastic’ match-winner Jackson Enzo Maresca is not concerned by the form of Marc Guéhi despite the defender costing his side three goals in the past two Premier League matches, the Manchester City manager said after seeing his side lose in the league for the first time this season. Nicolas Jackson’s double earned Aston Villa a 2-1 victory at Villa Park after Guéhi was unable to control the ball for the opener. Instead he spilled it into the path of John McGinn, who played it to Jackson, allowing him to score the first of two goals. The defender was then substituted at half-time having been booked on 32 minutes. Guéhi’s errors allowed Ipswich to score twice against City last weekend. Continue reading...

item.description: Manchester City added a loss in the Premier League to one to the Premier League, as their perfect record this season vanished without an independent commission in sight. Two of the most in-form strikers in England did battle and it was Nicolas Jackson’s double that meant his side came out on top against Erling Haaland. City are certainly fallible, losing for the fourth time in a row here, and it was a reminder that life will not always be as simple as their first seven games. Mistakes cost City as Marc Guéhi and Gianluigi Donnarumma were punished by Jackson, who will have taken great pleasure in ending the winning run of his former Chelsea manager Enzo Maresca. item.title: Vincent Kompany to miss ‘weeks, not days’ with virus treatment, say Bayern Munich
item.description: Head coach in hospital after collapsing in training Assistant coach Aaron Danks to take charge against Freiburg Bayern Munich expect Vincent Kompany to miss an extended period as their head coach continues his hospital treatment for a virus after collapsing on the training pitch on Friday. Speaking at a press conference on Saturday, Bayern’s sporting director, Max Eberl, confirmed Kompany was still in hospital in a stable condition. Kompany’s English assistant coach, Aaron Danks, will replace the 40-year-old for Sunday’s Bundesliga match at Freiburg. Eberl said examinations were continuing to determine the nature of the former Manchester City and Belgium captain’s condition, with a recovery timeframe yet to be determined. Continue reading...

item.title: Enciso rescues point in storm for Ipswich to deny Nottingham Forest
item.description: Amid a Suffolk squall, winds whipping, a constant drum of rain, an encounter full of half-chances, mistakes, the obligatory refereeing controversy and searching questions. Do Ipswich possess the stones to deal with the big league? Perhaps so. How long can Nottingham Forest’s dip sustain before their president, Evangelos Marinakis, takes his usual course of action. Perhaps not much longer. Ipswich’s Gary O’Neil was the happier manager, Forest had created the cleaner opportunities, only for familiar failings to cost them. “We were never quite good enough with the ball to turn it into a football match,” said O’Neil. Further adding to Forest’s disappointment, Ipswich’s Issa Diop escaped what looked, on first glance, a red card for a last-man foul. A first-half exchange of goals, both owing much to defensive laxness, determined the result. Continue reading...

item.title: Change captain? Play the kids? How to solve the problems at Manchester United
item.description: The beleaguered Michael Carrick’s job is on the line, but there are steps he can take to revive the stricken club The big question as Bournemouth arrive for Sunday’s 2pm kick-off at Old Trafford is whether Michael Carrick will show his authority by stripping the captaincy from Bruno Fernandes and/or dropping Manchester United’s five-times player of the year. On Friday, Carrick refused to deny he may do so, but the bigger picture concerns whether cashing in on the Portuguese and his fellow mutineer, Lisandro Martínez, in the winter window would be prescient to initiate a new era. Fernandes and Martínez are out of contract in the close season (the club has an extra year’s option in both cases) and, judging by recent behaviour, intend to leave. So yielding, say, £40m and £25m respectively for them in January would allow investment as the rebuild begins. Even a few days on, Fernandes’s words in Como seem incredible: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation. Fernandes’s open questioning of the tactics is a challenge to the head coach’s authority and we wait to see how/if Carrick will face it down. If Carrick acts and proves he is not a lame duck then even if he is removed a favour is done for his successor. Continue reading...

item.content:encoded: The beleaguered Michael Carrick’s job is on the line, but there are steps he can take to revive the stricken club The big question as Bournemouth arrive for Sunday’s 2pm kick-off at Old Trafford is whether Michael Carrick will show his authority by stripping the captaincy from Bruno Fernandes and/or dropping Manchester United’s five-times player of the year. On Friday, Carrick refused to deny he may do so, but the bigger picture concerns whether cashing in on the Portuguese and his fellow mutineer, Lisandro Martínez, in the winter window would be prescient to initiate a new era. Fernandes and Martínez are out of contract in the close season (the club has an extra year’s option in both cases) and, judging by recent behaviour, intend to leave. So yielding, say, £40m and £25m respectively for them in January would allow investment as the rebuild begins. Even a few days on, Fernandes’s words in Como seem incredible: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation. Fernandes’s open questioning of the tactics is a challenge to the head coach’s authority and we wait to see how/if Carrick will face it down. If Carrick acts and proves he is not a lame duck then even if he is removed a favour is done for his successor. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Mourinho is ready for his clásico return – stock up on popcorn, folks!
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jr doesn’t have a body double and Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh. Like all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recent piece in The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. Odd reference points these billionaires” – Noble Francis. May I be the first of 1,057 Daniels to say thank you for the good luck message at the end of Thursday’s Football Daily. It has put a little extra pep in my step today” – Daniel Mee. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: Mamdani loves Arsenal. He should challenge them to cut ties with the UAE over Sudan | Sasha Lezhnev and John Prendergast
item.description: The New York mayor’s passion for the Gunners and human rights presents an opportunity to push back on the club’s lucrative UAE sponsorship Like him or not, there is no doubt that New York mayor Zohran Mamdani’s passion for certain issues is electric, and that passion played a large part in him getting elected. But today, two of his biggest passions are on a collision course. On one hand, Mamdani is now arguably the US’s most high-profile supporter of English Premier League champions Arsenal. A superfan since he was a child , he has put the Gunners into the American spotlight more than anyone since becoming mayor. The Empire State Building gleamed in Arsenal’s red and white when they won the Premier League title. He wrote an essay about what Arsenal’s championship means to him, talks about Arsenal at press conferences and interviews and inaugurated Thierry Henry Way near Times Square in honor of the Arsenal legend. Continue reading...

item.title: Crystal Palace and Newcastle face off with both in search of season kickstart
item.description: Pierre Sage and Matthias Jaissle face some key questions: both were appointed this summer yet form, and results, have proved elusive Conceding 17 goals in seven Premier League matches is not exactly the start Pierre Sage or Crystal Palace’s hierarchy would have hoped for. The transition from Oliver Glasner’s counterattacking 3-4-2-1 formation to the Frenchman’s more aggressive approach has exposed massive weaknesses in defence, culminating with last week’s humiliating defeat at Brighton. Palace fans became used to success under Glasner and they are already looking nervously over their shoulders at the bottom three. Even their league wins under Sage so far – against Fulham and Nottingham Forest – could have ended in defeat. Something doesn’t seem right in south London. EA Continue reading...

item.title: Pascal Gross: the obsessive runner keeping Brighton ‘one step ahead’ after fast start
item.description: Midfielder ‘who can never stand still’ has brought renewed energy to Seagulls since return to the club in January Most footballers like to spend their summers unwinding after a long season but not Pascal Gross. Having been part of the Germany squad eliminated in the quarter-finals of Euro 2024 , the midfielder entered – and won – a running race. Gross completed the 8.4km course on Juist, in the East Frisian islands, in 31 minutes and 35 seconds. He is not known as someone who courts attention, and his victory by more than a minute came to light only when a video was posted on social media by a competitor. Continue reading...

item.title: Is el clásico still the world’s biggest match? Three questions before Barcelona v Real Madrid
item.description: The fixture’s relevance waned as the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded. Can Lamine Yamal and Mbappé lift it into a new era? For the best part of a decade, el clásico was more than just soccer’s biggest fixture. It was the defining narrative. At the peak of the Lionel Messi v Cristiano Ronaldo era, there were clásicos everywhere. Yes, when the two historic rivals clashed on the pitch, but also in the voting for the Ballon d’Or every year and in so much of the discourse around the sport. As the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded, though, so too did the clásico ’s relevance. This isn’t to say matches between Barcelona and Real Madrid no longer matter. They always have and always will. In 2026, however, it’s difficult to measure a clásico ’s standing. Is it still the sport’s biggest fixture? Continue reading...

item.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
item.description: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. Niall McVeigh Ipswich v Nottingham Forest, Friday 8pm BST Aston Villa v Manchester City, Saturday 12.30pm BST Arsenal v Everton, Saturday 3pm BST Coventry v Fulham, Saturday 3pm BST Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Post-Ferguson worn-out horror show continues at Manchester United
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! We’re in the midst of what the kids call “spooky season” – or, for our fellow fusty old-timers out there, “autumn”. If you’ve been cosying up with a few horror flicks this month, you’ll know nothing good can come from hanging around a lake at this time of year. And so it proved for Manchester United, who endured an early Halloween nightmare on the banks of Lake Como that may have driven a stake through the Michael Carrick era. Hailed as the interim anti-Amorim not so long ago, Carrick has overseen two wins this season, against Ipswich and Sabah Baku . Como were in Serie D when Carrick won Big Cup with United as a player in 2008 – now, 18 years on, he watched the Italian upstarts dance, twirl and shimmy through the set of training cones he had sent out to represent his storied club. Any chance the Independent Football Regulator could also force the sale of Manchester United while it is at it? – James Marriott. Belated birthday greetings to Florent Sinama-Pongolle, a player once described (by Big Website if memory serves) as the only footballer whose surname sounds like an art-house trend – Alan Burgess. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Niall McVeigh
item.content:encoded: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! We’re in the midst of what the kids call “spooky season” – or, for our fellow fusty old-timers out there, “autumn”. If you’ve been cosying up with a few horror flicks this month, you’ll know nothing good can come from hanging around a lake at this time of year. And so it proved for Manchester United, who endured an early Halloween nightmare on the banks of Lake Como that may have driven a stake through the Michael Carrick era. Hailed as the interim anti-Amorim not so long ago, Carrick has overseen two wins this season, against Ipswich and Sabah Baku . Como were in Serie D when Carrick won Big Cup with United as a player in 2008 – now, 18 years on, he watched the Italian upstarts dance, twirl and shimmy through the set of training cones he had sent out to represent his storied club. Any chance the Independent Football Regulator could also force the sale of Manchester United while it is at it? – James Marriott. Belated birthday greetings to Florent Sinama-Pongolle, a player once described (by Big Website if memory serves) as the only footballer whose surname sounds like an art-house trend – Alan Burgess. item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Dwight Yorke: ‘I’m not a kid trying to get into management – I’m a manager’
item.description: Ghana may soon come calling for Trinidad and Tobago’s former captain and manager, who is proud of his CV since his days as a Premier League striker Dwight Yorke wants you to stop calling him a former player. “I’m not a kid trying to get into management for the first time,” he says from his home in Dubai. “I’ve done that and I want that message to come across clearly.” The message has a deadline. Carlos Queiroz left his job as Ghana head coach on 1 October and the Ghana Football Association is searching for his successor. Yorke is among the names under consideration, along with Pape Thiaw, Aliou Cissé and Walid Regragui, the former Morocco head coach, according to Ghanaian media. Continue reading...

item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . Continue reading...

item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: WSL talking points: pressure mounts on Slegers as Hemp closes on record
item.description: Another round of games and another disappointing draw for Arsenal while Manchester City sit top of the table with a 100% record There would have been hope that the international break could offer the Arsenal players and staff a reset but the same problems reared their head at the Emirates on Sunday in a 1-1 draw with Birmingham. As they have done so often this season, the Gunners dominated most attacking and possession-based metrics – they registered 76% possession, a 2.73 xG and 43 touches in the opposition box – but their profligacy in front of goal and lack of urgency in their play once again came to the fore. Of their 27 chances, they managed just four on target as they toiled against a resilient opposition who understood the playbook. Birmingham set up in a strong defensive structure, protecting their box admirably with numbers to frustrate Renée Slegers’s side, who famously struggle to break down low blocks. In contrast, Birmingham scored with their one shot on target as Océane Hurtré took her impressive tally to six in six. Sophie Downey Match report: Arsenal 1-1 Birmingham Continue reading...

Here we have the man who hired the man. The man who fires the man. The man who also hired or rehired the previous two men he had to fire. Berrada was poached from Manchester City on the basis of his ability to grow commercial revenue (yes, OK, stop laughing), and appears, like everyone else with any actual reach around here, to exist in a strangely consequence-free bubble. item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. Continue reading...

item.title: Transfer window verdict: how every Premier League club fared
item.description: The British transfer record was equalled and one club signed no fewer than 18 players in another hectic summer Bringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run? They began targeting Morgan Rogers before pivoting to Vinícius Júnior when the England forward went to Chelsea, only to end up disappointed when Vinícius signed a new deal with Real Madrid. Julián Alvarez made clear he had no intention of joining from Atlético Madrid in the final days of the window and Arsenal kept their powder dry despite sanctioning the exits of Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Ethan Nwaneri to Borussia Dortmund. Should Gabriel Martinelli complete his move to Al-Hilal as expected in the coming days – the Saudi Pro League window remains open – a few injuries could leave Arteta short. Ed Aarons Continue reading...

item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...

item.title: Aitana Bonmatí makes Guardian top 100 history with third title in a row
item.description: The margin may have got smaller but the brilliant Spanish midfielder makes it a hat-trick of No 1 finishes They say the best things come in threes, and Aitana Bonmatí has written herself into the Guardian’s top 100 history as the first player to finish at the top of the tree for a third consecutive year. Last year the majestic midfielder emulated her Barcelona and Spain teammate Alexia Putellas by winning for a second year running , but the 27-year-old has now gone one better, establishing herself once again at the top of the women’s game. Continue reading...

item.title: Sign up for the Moving the Goalposts newsletter: our free women’s football email
item.description: Get our roundup of women’s football for free twice a week, featuring the insights of experts such as Ada Hegerberg and Magdalena Eriksson Join us as we delve deeper into the wonderful world of women’s football in our weekly newsletter. It is informative, entertaining, global, critical – when needed – and, above all, passionate. Written mainly by Júlia Belas Trindade and Sophie Downey , expect guest appearances from stars such as Anita Asante, Ada Hegerberg and many more.
